World-class bioprocess consumable franchise with deep regulatory switching costs, but management committed severe capital allocation errors: debt-financing the €2.4B Polyplus acquisition at top-of-cycle multiples, blowing leverage past 4.5x EBITDA, and diluting shareholders with a €1B emergency equity raise.
column21: Gross margins exceed 50% with high recurring single-use consumable mix. However, management overleveraged the company into the bioprocess downturn via €2.4B Polyplus deal (€3B bond issuance at 4.4-4.9%), driving net debt/EBITDA >4.5x in 2023 and triggering a dilutive €1B equity capital increase in Q1 2024.

column14: Lab automation software and OEM diagnostics components have switching costs, but low pricing power in OEM contract manufacturing (Paramit) and cyclical lab instrument capex depress multi-year ROIC to ~7-8% (and negative with 2025 impairment), failing the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Respected Swiss lab-automation engineer, but high exposure to cyclical lab instrument capex and lower-margin contract manufacturing (Paramit) compressed adjusted margins to 16% and triggered a CHF 140M goodwill impairment, leaving multi-year ROIC well below the 12% hurdle.
column21: Adjusted EBITDA margins compressed from 20.5% (2023) to 16.1% (2025). The $1.0B acquisition of Paramit diluted returns and caused a CHF 139.5M goodwill write-down in 2025 (CHF -110.7M net loss). Multi-year ROIC hovers around 7-8%, well beneath the 12% threshold.

column14: Global monopoly in sublingual allergy immunotherapy tablets (SLIT). Proprietary biological extract standardization, multi-year clinical trial registries, and EMA/FDA approvals create near-impenetrable barriers; GAAP ROIC has scaled to 23.7% with strong pricing power across Western reimbursement systems.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global monopoly in allergy immunotherapy tablets (SLIT) with biological extraction know-how, deep regulatory moats, expanding EBIT margins (>26%), and a fortress net-cash balance sheet. [5-10Y g: tablet volume growth 5.0% + North American/international adoption 2.0% + price/mix 1.0% + share repurchases 0.5%]
column21: Operating ROIC reaches 20.4% (FY25 GAAP ROIC 23.7%) with 101.5% FCF conversion. Balance sheet has DKK 1,089M net cash and interest coverage >50x. Proprietary allergen standardization and 3-year patient adherence regimens generate high-margin recurring cash flows.

column14: Leading oncology and rare disease patent estate, but 5-year median GAAP ROIC is sub-hurdle (~9-10%), and pricing power is severely curtailed by US IRA Medicare price negotiations (Farxiga), European single-payer price caps, and late-decade patent expirations.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & Pricing Power, REJECT). Premier oncology innovator, but multi-year GAAP ROIC averages ~9-10% (diluted by the $39B Alexion buyout) and pricing power faces severe headwinds from US IRA Medicare price cuts (Farxiga), European healthcare budget freezes, and upcoming patent cliffs.
column21: GAAP ROIC hovered between 4% and 12% from 2022 to 2024, with 5-year median ROIC failing the 12% threshold. Pricing power is actively constrained by legislative price caps (IRA Farxiga price cuts), European cost-containment, and upcoming loss of exclusivity on key franchise blockbusters.

column14: Patents in crop traits and pharmaceuticals exist, but commodity generic competition collapsed glyphosate pricing, while multi-billion litigation expenses and asset write-downs keep ROCE/ROIC negative (-1.4%), completely failing Gate 3b.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & Negative Returns, REJECT). Crop science and pharma conglomerate crippled by the disastrous $63B Monsanto acquisition: ongoing multi-billion US glyphosate litigation, generic pricing collapse in herbicides, Xarelto patent cliff, and negative group ROCE (-1.4%).
column21: Reported net losses of €-2.9B (2023), €-2.5B (2024), and €-3.6B (2025). ROCE remained depressed at 0.7% (2023), -0.1% (2024), and -1.4% (2025) with >€3.7B in Crop Science impairments and severe generic pricing deflation in glyphosate.

column14: Vaccine pricing power is constrained by public health tender procurement and advisory recommendations (e.g. CDC ACIP), while the flagship dolutegravir HIV franchise faces an impending patent cliff in 2028-2029.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC averages 9-11%, failing the 12% hurdle across the cycle. Vaccine pricing is heavily constrained by institutional tender bodies and CDC ACIP guidelines, while the core dolutegravir HIV franchise faces patent expiration and generic erosion in 2028-2029.
column21: Historical GAAP ROIC over 10 years has hovered around 9-11% across the cycle (2021: ~9.5%, 2024: ~9.6%), failing the 12% threshold. Dolutegravir-based regimens (Tivicay, Triumeq, Dovato) generate ~20% of group revenue (£6B+) and face loss of exclusivity in the US in 2028 and Europe in 2029. Vaccine revenues face institutional price caps and advisory narrowing (e.g. ACIP RSV recommendation adjustments), preventing sustained pricing power >= inflation.

column14: Generic injectable and oral solid markets are characterized by multi-source commodity competition and chronic price deflation imposed by consolidated hospital GPOs and wholesalers, leaving Hikma without proprietary pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3a (Moat Archetype: None) and Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Generic hospital injectables and oral formulations face chronic price deflation from consolidated US hospital purchasing consortia (GPOs) and wholesalers, preventing sustained pricing power above inflation.
column21: Hikma generates the majority of operating profits from US generic injectables and oral solid generics, where absence of patent exclusivity exposes products to competitive generic bidding and structural price deflation. While core ROIC has historically been ~16-17% through manufacturing scale, the business model lacks a structural moat archetype (3a=None) and cannot unilaterally raise prices at or above inflation without losing volume.

column14: Orphan drug exclusivities in oncology and neuroscience provide niche defensibility, but flagship blockbuster Somatuline faces ongoing generic lanreotide erosion while European health authorities enforce statutory price controls.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Specialty pharmaceutical model is heavily reliant on Somatuline, which faces accelerating generic competition in the US and Europe, while European single-payer price controls prevent sustained pricing power >= inflation.
column21: Somatuline historically accounted for over 35% of group revenue and the core of operating earnings, but its primary patents have expired and generic lanreotide alternatives have entered key markets. While Core Operating Margin remains ~32% and ROIC ~15%, the lack of volume-insulated pricing power against generic substitution and heavy reliance on external M&A (e.g. Albireo, Epizyme) fail the Munger moat durability standard.

column14: Conglomerate structure across cyclical electronic chemicals, life science tools, and mid-tier pharma lacks an overarching moat; 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 9.0% falls well short of the 12% hurdle due to heavy historical acquisition goodwill.
column20: Fails Gate 3a (Moat Archetype: None) and Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 9.0% falls well below the 12% hurdle, burdened by €25B+ in acquisition goodwill, while cyclical electronics specialty chemicals lack pricing power.
column21: GAAP ROIC has steadily declined from 10.56% in FY2022 to 8.27% in FY2025 (median 9.03%), reflecting persistent balance sheet dilution from historical mega-acquisitions (Sigma-Aldrich, Versum). The electronics materials division is exposed to cyclical semiconductor demand fluctuations, and Life Science faced customer destocking, preventing the business from demonstrating sustained pricing power >= inflation.

column14: Innovative patent estate in radioligands and biologics, but core revenue generator Entresto lost US patent exclusivity in mid-2025 triggering immediate multi-generic competition, alongside mandatory US Medicare IRA price negotiations.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Blockbuster Entresto lost US patent exclusivity in mid-2025 leading to immediate multi-source generic launches, while mandatory Medicare IRA price cuts and European single-payer price controls eliminate pricing power above inflation.
column21: While post-Sandoz ROIC expanded to ~24-25%, top-selling blockbuster Entresto (~$6B+ sales, ~15% of revenue) suffered US patent litigation losses clearing immediate generic market entry in mid-2025, triggering double-digit revenue erosion. With key products subject to mandatory CMS Maximum Fair Price caps under the IRA and European statutory price cuts, Novartis cannot unilaterally raise prices at or above inflation without volume loss.

column14: World-class protein engineering and sterile manufacturing scale, but US net realized prices are eroding under heavy PBM rebate escalation with Eli Lilly, compounding pharmacy copycats, and mandatory Medicare IRA price negotiations.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Despite elite ROIC, net realized GLP-1 pricing is under structural erosion from fierce PBM rebate concessions against Eli Lilly, compounding pharmacy substitution, mandatory Medicare IRA price negotiations, and a 35-50% US list price cut.
column21: Novo Nordisk exhibits exceptional ROIC (62% median) and cash flow, but net realized pricing per patient in its core US market is eroding due to gross-to-net PBM rebate pressures and intense competition with Eli Lilly's tirzepatide. The company announced 35-50% cuts to US list prices for Wegovy and Ozempic effective 2027, alongside mandatory CMS price caps under the Inflation Reduction Act, disqualifying it from passing Gate 3b pricing power >= inflation.

column14: While Orion captures high-margin tiered royalties from Bayer for Nubeqa (darolutamide), its broader business comprises Nordic generics, mature pharmaceuticals, and animal health subject to mandatory reference pricing, tender competition, and ongoing price erosion. Orion lacks systemic pricing power >= inflation across its portfolio, and corporate earnings are overly dependent on a single partnered oncology molecule facing generic challenges and eventual patent expiration.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (N, REJECT). Orion's operating profits are heavily concentrated in Nubeqa royalties licensed to Bayer, while its core base in Nordic generics and mature pharmaceuticals faces persistent price erosion and state reference pricing caps, precluding genuine pricing power >= inflation.
column21: Historical ROCE fluctuated between 25% and 45% boosted by Nubeqa milestones and royalties from Bayer. However, core generic and consumer health divisions suffer continuous price erosion in European markets. Single-asset royalty concentration leaves the company without a self-sustaining, multi-product R&D pricing moat.

column14: Price controls across Southern European national health systems restrict pricing power on mature primary care portfolio. Despite expanding into rare diseases (Enjaymo, Signifor), single-payer statutory reimbursement caps and mandatory price cuts prevent pricing power >= inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (N, REJECT). Specialty pharmaceutical group operating under European national healthcare price controls. Statutory price cuts across its primary care base prevent passing through inflation, while growth relies on debt-funded orphan drug roll-up acquisitions.
column21: GAAP ROIC averages ~14% supported by specialty pharma acquisitions (EUSA, Enjaymo), but tangible equity is negative (-€1.27B against €3.19B of intangibles/goodwill) with long-term debt of €2.13B. European single-payer pricing dynamics restrict organic pricing power >= inflation.

column14: Global leader in in-vitro diagnostics and proprietary oncology/neurology biologics. Installed instrument base creates high switching costs and recurring reagent toll booths, while proprietary Genentech antibody platform delivers continuous replacement blockbusters (Vabysmo, Ocrevus, Hemlibra) with resilient global pricing power.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global diagnostics and biologic medicine powerhouse with high switching costs in closed-reagent instruments, founder family stewardship, and 28% GAAP ROIC. Balance sheet fortress with 13.6x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: diagnostics reagent volume 3.5% + innovative biologics volume 3.0% - legacy patent cliff erosion -1.5% + dividend yield 2.5% + buybacks 0.5%]
column21: 27.6% 5-year median GAAP ROIC (FY2022: 31.8%, FY2023: 28.4%, FY2024: 19.7%, FY2025: 26.8%), Tangible ROIC >50%. FY2025 Owner FCF of CHF 14.6B (113% FCF/NI conversion). FY2025 Owner EPS (CHF 16.04) surpassed prior peak. Net debt / NI is ~1.7x with 13.6x EBIT/interest coverage.

column14: Sub-hurdle capital efficiency with 5-year median GAAP ROIC of only 7.45%, well below the 12% hurdle. While Dupixent is a commercial success in immunology, historical legacy acquisitions have bloated the asset base (goodwill and intangibles of €67.6B), and upcoming 2031 Dupixent patent expiration creates severe concentration risk without adequate organic R&D return proof.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (N, REJECT). Sanofi fails the empirical proof-of-moat test with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of only 7.45% (hurdle >= 12%), burdened by €67.6B in capitalized intangibles/goodwill from dilutive historical M&A and facing severe concentration risk ahead of Dupixent's 2031 patent cliff.
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 7.45% (FY2022: 10.9%, FY2023: 7.4%, FY2024: 7.5%, FY2025: 7.1%), failing the 12% hurdle. Intangibles and goodwill total €67.6B against €71.4B in equity, reflecting massive historical capital deployment that fails to generate super-normal economic returns.

column14: Commodity off-patent generics and biosimilars manufacturer facing continuous annual low-to-mid single digit price deflation, tender bidding, and government reference price cuts. Sandoz possesses zero pricing power >= inflation across its core volume base.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (N, REJECT). Pure-play generic and biosimilar drug manufacturer subject to structural price deflation and competitive tender bidding. Lacks pricing power >= inflation across its commodity pharmaceuticals portfolio.
column21: Spun off from Novartis in late 2023. Core generics portfolio suffers persistent low-to-mid single-digit annual price erosion from competitive tenders and payer price cuts. While biosimilar volume grows, structural commodity price dynamics in off-patent drugs preclude real pricing power.

column14: Sub-hurdle multi-cycle capital efficiency with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of only 7.67% (failing the 12% hurdle). Although the recent launch of Bimzelx (bimekizumab) in immunology boosted FY2025 earnings, historical acquisitions (such as Zogenix) and ongoing generic erosion across legacy epilepsy drugs (Vimpat) keep full-cycle capital returns below the Munger quality threshold.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (N, REJECT). Multi-cycle capital efficiency fails the Munger bar with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of only 7.67% (hurdle >= 12%). While Bimzelx provides recent growth, single-product concentration and generic erosion of legacy CNS franchises dilute full-cycle returns.
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 7.67% (FY2022: 4.47%, FY2023: 4.19%, FY2024: 10.87%, FY2025: 15.19%), failing the 12% hurdle. Intangibles and goodwill of €8.54B constitute the vast majority of €10.87B in equity, reflecting high acquisition capital intensity that suppresses multi-cycle returns.

column14: Unmatched commercial narrowbody backlog (A320neo family) with over 8,500 aircraft on order provides commanding commercial aircraft pricing power.

Global commercial aircraft duopolist with decade-long backlog, but fails peak-to-peak business cycle compounding (2024 EPS of €5.36 remains below 2018 peak of €5.80+) alongside chronic supply-chain working capital volatility and recurring defense/space contract write-downs.

column20: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Premier French combat aircraft manufacturer with world-class engineering, but rejected at Gate 6 due to violent working capital volatility (+€4.9B in 2022 to -€1.2B in 2023) driven by lumpy sovereign export downpayments and cyclical Falcon business jet exposure.
column21: Exceptional engineering culture and fortress net cash (€8.4B available cash in 2024), but free cash flow fluctuates wildly (+€4.9B in FY22 vs -€1.2B in FY23) due to milestone advances on export Rafale contracts and discretionary Falcon business jet delivery cycles, failing steady cash conversion standards.

Indispensable UK defense prime with sovereign submarine monopoly, but rejected at Gate 6 as net debt surged to £4.95B following the debt-funded $5.5B Ball Aerospace acquisition alongside legacy pension obligations and through-cycle ROIC below 9%.

column14: Sole-source UK naval dockyard operator (Devonport) with long-term Partnering Agreements supporting continuous nuclear submarine maintenance and refits.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Strategic UK naval dockyard operator, but rejected at Gate 6 due to razor-thin operating margins (4-5%), chronic fixed-price contract disputes/write-downs (>£300M in cumulative losses on Type 31 frigates), and volatile cash conversion.
column21: Devonport dockyard provides critical naval support, but contract execution volatility is chronic: Type 31 frigate program incurred >£300M in cumulative losses and required a formal Dispute Resolution Process with the UK MoD. Statutory operating margins remain compressed at 4-5%.

Newly listed on Euronext Amsterdam in January 2026 with no public multi-cycle operating history; complex holding structure built via rapid debt-funded defense rollups across Central Europe and the US, with key operational risks—including undisclosed NATO procurement suspensions at its Spanish subsidiary and ongoing state contract corruption probes—invisible from reported financials.
column21: Czechoslovak Group (CSG N.V.) debuted on Euronext Amsterdam in January 2026, lacking any public multi-cycle operating record. Employs an aggressive acquisition rollup strategy (The Kinetic Group, Fiocchi). Faces severe transparency and governance concerns: NATO NSPA quietly suspended subsidiary Fábrica de Municiones de Granada (FMG) in July 2025 (undisclosed at IPO), and state consulting payments to Slovakia's defense minister triggered public anti-corruption inquiries.

column14: High pricing power on sole-source radar and sensor components (Eurofighter, TRML-4D, airborne electronic warfare) for Western defense platforms.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Premier German defense sensor, radar, and optronics specialist, but fails Gate 6 due to debt-funded M&A (ESG Group acquisition driving net debt to ~€650M+) and heavy working capital absorption during defense production ramp-ups.
column21: High-spec defense sensor provider with strong Eurofighter and air defense exposure. However, 2024 ESG Group acquisition increased net debt to ~€650M-€700M, and FCF dropped to €112M under intensive working capital requirements, while GAAP ROIC remains constrained around 10-11%.

column14: Sovereign defense electronics (AESA radars, sonar arrays, C4ISR) and certified civil avionics/ATM protected by national security clearances and high switching costs. Defense procurement contracts feature contractual inflation indexation.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Cash conversion and structural space division drag). While defense electronics and avionics possess defensible moats, chronic restructuring losses in commercial space satellites (Thales Alenia Space) and lumpy multi-year contract working capital fail the Munger cash compounding and predictability bar.
column21: Thales Alenia Space faces ongoing structural disruption from low-Earth orbit satellite constellations, resulting in restructuring charges and margin dilution. Large sovereign defense contracts generate volatile milestone working capital swings across reporting periods, impairing steady cash flow predictability despite solid top-line defense demand.

column14: Roughly half of Indra's revenue stems from Minsait, a commoditized IT consulting and software development business facing intense competition, low pricing power, and rising wage inflation. 5-year average ROIC (~11.5%) falls short of the 12% hurdle. High customer concentration in competitive Spanish public sector tenders.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat Archetype 'None', ROIC < 12%). Roughly 50% of revenue stems from Minsait, a commoditized IT services and consulting business lacking durable pricing power. 5-year average ROIC (~11.5%) fails the 12% hurdle, compounded by heavy state governance interference from SEPI.
column21: 5-year average ROIC of ~11.5% (7.0% in 2021, 9.5% in 2022) falls short of the 12% hurdle. Minsait constitutes ~50% of revenue in low-margin, billable-hour IT consulting vulnerable to wage inflation and margin erosion. Defense contracts are heavily concentrated in Spanish government procurement subject to political intervention by state-owned SEPI (25%+ owner).

column14: Dominant technological monopolies including JSM (sole internal cruise missile for F-35), NSM anti-ship missile adopted across NATO, and NASAMS air defense. Unsurpassed pricing power confirmed by 32%+ ROIC.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Norway's premier defense and maritime technology champion with dominant missile monopolies, 32% ROIC, and massive net cash fortress. [5-10Y g: missile system deliveries 6.0% + NASAMS air defense 3.0% + maritime automation 1.5% + buybacks/dividends 0.5% - cycle normalization 1.0%]
column21: Median ROIC of 32.1% and operating ROIC of 72.6%. Owner EPS compounded from NOK 3.37 in 2022 to NOK 9.04 in 2025 (39% CAGR). Multi-year FCF conversion exceeds 140% with NOK 11.0B Owner FCF in FY2025. Balance sheet holds NOK 20.2B in cash against just NOK 1.0B in debt (net cash NOK 19.2B). Order backlog exceeds NOK 157B driven by sole-source JSM (F-35), NSM, and NASAMS.

column14: Pricing power in military helicopters (AgustaWestland AW139, AW101) and defense electronics, though dragged down by commercial aerostructures subcontracts.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Aerostructures cash burn and volatile defense working capital). While military helicopters and defense electronics hold strong market positions, chronic aerostructures cash drains and lumpy defense project working capital fail the Munger cash compounding and balance sheet peace-of-mind test.
column21: Aerostructures division has been a chronic drag on margins and cash generation due to low-margin subcontracts (e.g. Boeing 787 fuselage). Multi-cycle ROIC has historically lingered below cost of capital (3-7%), while defense contract working capital lumpiness generates volatile operating cash flows.

column14: Contractually locked aftermarket Risk and Revenue Sharing Partnerships (RRSPs) on commercial aircraft engines (GTF, GEnx, Trent) provide long-term high-margin aftermarket toll booth revenues with pricing power indexed above inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (FCF conversion < 80% and negative multi-year statutory earnings). GKN Aerospace engine RRSP toll booth has strong sole-source positions, but negative multi-year statutory earnings (£-1.02B in 2023, £-49M in 2024) and cash outflows from GTF powdered metal fleet inspections fail the Munger cash compounding and balance sheet peace-of-mind test.
column21: Statutory net income was negative across 2022 (-£308M), 2023 (-£1,020M), and 2024 (-£49M) before recovering to £370M in 2025. Free cash flow was negative in 2023 and 2024 (-£74M) before turning positive to £125M in 2025, failing the multi-year 80% FCF conversion requirement. Significant cash outflows required for Pratt & Whitney GTF engine fleet inspections and airline compensation.

column14: Toll booth on commercial aviation fleet through long-term Risk and Revenue Sharing Partnerships (RRSPs) and independent MRO network. High switching costs and certified proprietary spare parts deliver pricing power indexed above inflation, proven by multi-cycle ROIC > 16%.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Premier German aircraft engine innovator and commercial MRO toll booth with high switching costs, low leverage, and 17% ROIC. [5-10Y g: commercial MRO shop visits 5.0% + spare parts volume 3.0% + pricing indexation 1.5% + buybacks 0.5% - GTF inspection headwind 1.0%]
column21: Median ROIC of 16.8% and operating ROIC of 27.2%, rebounding to 28.0% in 2025. Record 2025 performance with revenue of €8.76B (+16%), adjusted EBIT of €1.35B (+29%), and Owner EPS of €18.44. Balance sheet remains conservative with net debt under 1.0x EBITDA and interest coverage >12x. High switching costs across commercial engine RRSP programs (GTF, GE9X, CF6) and proprietary MRO network provide long-term inflation-indexed pricing power.

column14: Government defense testing and evaluation contractor facing sovereign monopsony clients (UK MoD, US DoD). Contracts are subject to single-source regulatory margin caps (SSRO baseline profit rate) or competitive bidding, leaving zero structural pricing power above inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (3a=None, 3b=N, REJECT). Defense testing and technical engineering contractor constrained by sovereign monopsony procurement frameworks and regulated margin caps. International IT/consulting operations face intense competition without pricing power.
column21: Operating margins structurally capped around 10-11% under UK Single Source Contract Regulations. Avantus Federal acquisition ($590M) expanded goodwill in hyper-competitive US government services without delivering pricing leverage. Low pricing power against sovereign defense ministries.

column14: Customized mission-critical tank transmissions (e.g. Leopard 2, Puma) create high engineering switching costs, but bargaining power rests with prime system integrators (KNDS, Rheinmetall) and sovereign defense agencies, resulting in a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 10.44% (sub-12% hurdle).
column20: Fails Gate 3 (3b=N, REJECT). Specialized defense transmission manufacturer fails the 12% multi-cycle GAAP ROIC hurdle (median 10.44%, 7.1-7.9% in 2022-2023) and lacks pricing power against prime contractors and defense ministries.
column21: 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 10.44% (2022: 7.9%, 2023: 7.1%, 2024: 13.0%, 2025: 15.2%). Triton PE carve-out left high net debt (€362M) relative to pre-2024 earnings. Pricing power is bounded by OEM primes (KNDS, Rheinmetall).

column14: Dominant European artillery munitions and combat vehicle manufacturer. Command of certified 155mm production lines, propellants (Nitrochemie), and Leopard/Boxer components provides formidable pricing power backed by a €60B+ order backlog.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (6=N, REJECT). Europe's land defense champion with dominant artillery munitions share, but multi-year FCF conversion falls short of the 80% threshold (~70% multi-year) due to heavy working capital expansion, long-cycle project inventories, and major factory capex.
column21: Multi-year FCF conversion 2018-2023 averaged ~69.5% of net income (below the 80% hurdle), impacted by substantial inventory builds and capex for ammunition manufacturing capacity. Net debt reached €1.24B in 2024. High defense backlog (€60B+) requires continuous heavy capital absorption.

column14: Sole-source engine supplier on the Airbus A350 (Trent XWB) and A330neo. Massive switching costs and regulatory barriers to entry. 15-25 year TotalCare LTSA contracts act as an ad valorem flying-hour toll booth where CEO Tufan Erginbilgic demonstrated formidable pricing power by renegotiating contracts and resetting spare parts pricing.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Widebody commercial aero engine monopoly on Airbus A350 with surging aftermarket cash flow, net cash balance sheet, and disciplined turnaround leadership. [5-10Y g: widebody flying hours 4.5% + LTSA price resets & escalation 2.5% + defense/power systems volume 2.0% + share buybacks 1.0%]
column21: Multi-cycle recovery from COVID trough to record operating profit (>£2.5B+ underlying) and >£3.5B FCF. Net cash position of £4.2B+ (Cash £6.0B vs Debt £1.8B). Sole-source engine position on Airbus A350 and A330neo with 15-25 year TotalCare LTSA cash-flow streams.

column14: Proprietary high-end defense electronics, radar systems, and tactical ground combat weapons (Carl-Gustaf, NLAW, AT4) with global NATO adoption. High barriers to entry and strong pricing power on proprietary munitions and Gripen life-cycle support.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (6=N, REJECT). Leading Nordic defense and tactical weapons champion, but multi-year FCF conversion structurally fails the 80% hurdle (~40-60%) due to heavy working capital absorption, milestone payment timing, and major capacity capex across Gripen and missile programs.
column21: Cumulative cash conversion targeted at only ~60% of EBIT by management. Historical FCF conversion to net income was ~68% in 2022, ~45% in 2023, and <30% in 2024. Long-cycle defense production (Gripen E, Kockums submarines, GlobalEye) absorbs significant working capital and capex.

column14: 50/50 CFM International JV with GE Aerospace commands ~75% narrowbody engine market share (100% sole-source on Boeing 737 MAX, ~60% on Airbus A320neo). 25-30 year airframe lifecycles create an unassailable high-margin aftermarket spare parts toll booth with proven pricing power above inflation.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Commercial aviation narrowbody engine duopoly with an unassailable 25-30 year aftermarket spare parts toll booth, net cash balance sheet, and 17%+ ROIC. [5-10Y g: commercial narrowbody flight hours 4.5% + LEAP aftermarket ramp & spares pricing 3.5% + defense/equipment 1.5% + net share buybacks 0.5% - supply chain friction 0.5%]
column21: 17%+ Operating ROIC. Consistent annual Owner FCF of €2.7B to €4.1B with >100% conversion of adjusted net income. Pristine net cash balance sheet (€6.8B cash vs €2.1B debt). Dominant narrowbody engine market share (~75% fleet share via CFM JV with GE) ensures decades of recurring spare parts cash flows.

column14: DHL Express possesses an elite global air hub-and-spoke network with significant scale economies shared and high TDI margins. However, consolidated group pricing power is severely impaired by Post & Parcel Germany, which is subject to statutory price caps by the German Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) and inflexible unionized labor costs, alongside the commoditized price-taker nature of Global Forwarding.
column20: Rejected at Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat). While DHL Express is a world-class global air express oligopolist with FedEx and UPS, the consolidated group remains burdened by Post & Parcel Germany, where statutory postal price caps from BNetzA and heavy collective bargaining wage settlements prevent inflation pass-through, while Global Forwarding operates as a cyclical freight rate price-taker.
column21: Group multi-year ROIC averages ~11-14%, dragged down by Post & Parcel Germany (ROIC ~9%) where BNetzA strictly limits stamp price increases despite ~11-12% union wage inflation and secular ~2-3% annual letter volume attrition. Global Forwarding gross profit swings violently with ocean/air spot freight rates.

column14: DSV is a best-in-class logistics consolidator with an unmatched M&A integration engine and asset-light scale economies shared. However, air and ocean forwarding remains an intermediary brokerage business where enterprise shippers multi-source and tender volume regularly with low switching costs, leaving DSV unable to exert autonomous pricing power >= inflation across the cycle without losing volume.
column20: Rejected at Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat). Although DSV possesses an exceptional acquisition integration playbook (crowned by the €14.3B DB Schenker transaction) and attractive asset-light capital efficiency, freight forwarding lacks structural switching costs. Shippers regularly tender routes on price, making DSV a price-taker on freight spreads without autonomous pricing power >= inflation.
column21: Reported pre-tax ROIC including goodwill ranges from 15% to 25%, but EBIT declined ~36% between 2022 and 2024 as pandemic-era freight premiums evaporated. Gross profit per unit is dictated by global shipping supply/demand balances rather than proprietary pricing power, and customer tender cycles ensure low customer lock-in.

column14: Kuehne+Nagel is the global #1 ocean freight forwarder and a top-3 air forwarder with scale economies shared and proprietary digital routing platforms (Seaexplorer). However, enterprise shippers face low switching costs and routinely tender shipping lanes across competing forwarders, leaving K+N as a price-taking intermediary without independent pricing power >= inflation across the freight cycle.
column20: Rejected at Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat). Kuehne+Nagel is an asset-light global forwarding leader with high return on equity and stable anchor ownership by Klaus-Michael Kühne. However, third-party logistics forwarding is structurally intermediated and subject to frequent customer RFQs; EBIT halved from 2022 peaks as global ocean/air freight spreads normalized, confirming that margins are market-driven rather than protected by proprietary pricing power.
column21: Group revenue declined from CHF 39.4B (2022) to CHF 23.8B (2023) and EBIT fell ~50% from CHF 3.76B to CHF 1.90B as abnormal pandemic supply-chain surcharges vanished. Core Sea and Air logistics volumes are re-tendered regularly by corporate customers on commodity freight rates with negligible customer lock-in.

column14: Groupe ADP operates an unreplicable infrastructure monopoly across the Greater Paris air basin (Paris-CDG, Paris-Orly, and Le Bourget). Physical runway slot scarcity and environmental restrictions prevent competing hub development. Under its dual-till regulatory model, non-aeronautical retail (Extime Paris luxury duty-free JV with Lagardère) exercises exceptional unregulated pricing power over high-spending intercontinental travelers, while aeronautical charges adjust via economic regulation agreements.
column20: Rejected at Gate 5 (Management & Capital Allocation, Score = 0). Paris CDG and Orly are irreplaceable national infrastructure assets, but Groupe ADP is 50.6% owned by the French State and suffers from acute capital allocation and governance pathologies: recurring regulatory conflict with ART over allowed aeronautical charges, bureaucratic inertia, and value-destructive international M&A (GMR Airports in India, TAV in Turkey) that loaded the balance sheet with €8.57B in net debt (>13x net income) and caused large impairment charges (€330M in 2024).
column21: State-dominated corporate governance has directed massive capital into speculative overseas airport stakes (GMR in India, TAV in Turkey) instead of disciplined per-share compounding. Net financial debt reached €8.57B at year-end 2024 against normalized net income of €638M (and reported net income of €342M, hit by a €330M merger charge on Indian assets), depressing consolidated ROIC to ~5-7%.

column14: Aena holds an unreplicable national spatial monopoly over 46 Spanish airports handling >99% of Spanish commercial air passenger traffic. High entry barriers (land acquisition, airspace constraints, environmental permitting) make competitive entry impossible. Pricing power is anchored by DORA regulatory inflation indexation on aeronautical tariffs and multi-year retail concession contracts with CPI-indexed Minimum Annual Guarantees (MAG). 5-year median ROIC of 16.5% proves moat durability. Main erosion risks stem from 5-year DORA regulatory resets and airline lobbying against tariff increases.
column20: Passes all 6 gates (Quality pass). Unreplicable statutory monopoly operating the entire Spanish commercial airport network, benefiting from Spain's structural status as the world's #2 tourist destination. Aeronautical tariffs protected by DORA inflation indexation, while commercial retail concessions (duty-free, F&B) deliver high-margin non-aero profit with minimum annual guarantees. 16.5% median ROIC, 98% FCF conversion, and strong balance sheet (Net Debt/NI 2.1x, interest coverage 12.3x). [5-10Y g: passenger volume 2.8% + tariff/commercial price 1.8% + commercial mix 0.8% - capex/D&A drag 0.4% + buybacks 0.0%]
column21: Multi-year GAAP ROIC expanded from 8.1% (2022) to 15.1% (2023), 17.9% (2024), and 18.3% (2025), averaging 16.5% median. 2025 Owner EPS of €1.4245 surpassed pre-pandemic peaks. FCF conversion stands at 97.7%. Net debt of €4.41B is 2.06x 2025 net income (€2.14B) with 12.3x EBIT interest coverage.

column14: Flughafen Zürich holds an irreplaceable infrastructure monopoly as Switzerland's primary gateway hub, operating under a federal concession valid through 2051. Severe geographical constraints in the Zurich basin and stringent environmental regulations make physical replication impossible. The model blends formulaic aeronautical tariffs with high-margin non-aero commercial retail and real estate (The Circle complex).
column20: Rejected at Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Zurich Airport is an irreplaceable physical infrastructure asset, aeronautical charges are governed by Swiss federal cost-plus return caps that hold multi-year ROIC to utility levels (~8.6%), while long-term runway growth is constrained by strict Swiss noise ordinances, a 23:00-06:00 curfew, contentious airspace negotiations with southern Germany, and high capex demands from the overseas Noida greenfield development in India.
column21: GAAP ROIC averages ~8.6% (6.05% in 2022, 8.61% in 2023, 9.05% in 2024, 8.60% in 2025), reflecting regulated utility-style asset return caps. Physical volume growth is tightly restricted by suburban noise politics and German airspace overflight restrictions, while heavy capex (CHF 550M-565M/yr) for domestic refurbishment and the Noida airport in India depresses free cash generation.

column14: Spec-in key systems installed base and decentralized acquisition machine. Unrivaled global scale in mechanical and digital access solutions (HID, Yale, effeff). Proven pricing power covering raw metal and wage inflation across multiple cycles. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 12.5% and operating tangible ROIC exceeds 100% due to serial acquisition intangibles.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in physical and electromechanical access solutions with an unassailable installed base in master key systems, architectural spec-in, and HID electronic credentials. Over two-thirds of revenue driven by resilient aftermarket maintenance and replacement. Proven pricing power across multiple inflationary cycles with multi-year FCF conversion >100%. [5-10Y g: aftermarket volume 2.0% + smart access mix 2.0% + pricing power 2.0% + bolt-on M&A 2.0% - restructuring drag 0.5% + buybacks 0.5%]
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 12.5% with tangible operating ROIC >100% due to capital-light assembly and large acquisition intangibles. Owner FCF conversion averaged 119.6% from 2022 to 2025 (FY2025 FCF of 18.6B SEK on 14.7B SEK net income). Net debt / NI sits at 3.07x with 6.98x interest coverage (EBIT 23.1B SEK vs 3.3B SEK interest), easily meeting the <4.0x leverage and >5.0x coverage thresholds.

column14: Decades of actuator precision engineering and distributor/OEM spec-in. Actuators are a minuscule cost component of building systems but carry catastrophic failure costs, cementing extreme customer loyalty and price insensitivity. Demonstrated multi-year median GAAP ROIC >32% and tangible ROIC >34%.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global undisputed hegemon in HVAC damper actuators and control valves. Unbeatable consumer surplus and installer trust: devices represent <2% of building HVAC capex but prevent millions in system downtime, resulting in supreme pricing power. Massive secular tailwinds from data-center liquid cooling and building decarbonization mandates. Pristine debt-free net cash balance sheet with >32% median ROIC. [5-10Y g: volume 5.0% + price 2.0% + data center cooling mix 2.0% - R&D/capex drag 0.5% + buybacks/dividends 0.0%]
column21: Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC consistently exceeds 27-36% (median 32.4%), with operating tangible ROIC of 34.2%. Owner EPS grew at a 13.9% CAGR from 2022 to 2025 (reaching 14.77 CHF peak in 2025). Long-term debt is 0.0 CHF against 100.6m CHF in cash, with EBIT / Interest coverage >270x.

column14: Installer loyalty and decades-evolved training ecosystem. Over 50% European market share in concealed cisterns. Behind-the-wall water damage risk creates insurmountable installer switching costs and pricing power. Multi-year median GAAP ROIC is 30.7% with tangible ROIC of 89.5% and sustained EBITDA margins above 30%.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Unrivaled European sanitary market hegemon (~50% share in concealed cisterns). Moat anchored by deep plumber installer loyalty, 29 specialized training academies, 50-year spare parts guarantees, and severe behind-the-wall leak liabilities that deter substitution. Maintained 30%+ EBITDA margins and >100% FCF conversion throughout the severe 2022-2025 European construction downturn. Fortress balance sheet with net debt <0.9x NI and interest coverage of 27x. [5-10Y g: European renovation volume 1.5% + pre-wall system penetration 1.5% + pricing power 2.0% - raw material/energy drag 0.5% + share repurchases 0.5%]
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 30.7% with operating tangible ROIC of 89.5%. Multi-year Owner FCF conversion averaged 107.0% (FY2025 FCF of 703.5m CHF on 597.8m CHF net income). Net debt is 505.2m CHF (0.84x NI) with 27.3x interest coverage (EBIT 762.5m CHF vs interest 27.9m CHF).

column14: Panel manufacturing scale and regulatory product certifications. Dense regional manufacturing network minimizes bulky freight costs. Demonstrated pricing power by passing through massive raw chemical (MDI/polyol/steel) cost inflation in 2021-2023. Multi-year median GAAP ROIC is 14.1% and operating tangible ROIC is 36.7%.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in high-performance insulated sandwich panels and advanced building envelopes. Structural moat derived from dense regional manufacturing footprint minimizing bulky transport costs, proprietary QuadCore formulations, and regulatory fire/thermal certifications. Resilient peak-to-peak EPS compounding across European construction cycles backed by EU building decarbonization regulations. Sound balance sheet with net debt of 2.2x NI and 12x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: building efficiency volume 3.5% + QuadCore/data center mix 2.5% + pricing power 2.0% - cyclical/capex drag 0.5% + buybacks 0.5%]
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 14.1% with operating tangible ROIC of 36.7%. Owner EPS compounded consistently from 3.27 EUR in 2022 to a peak of 3.67 EUR in 2025. Multi-year Owner FCF conversion reached 95.7%. Net debt / NI is 2.23x (1,495.8m EUR net debt vs 671.2m EUR NI) with interest coverage of 11.97x (EBIT 929.1m EUR vs interest 77.6m EUR).

column14: Fails Gate 3b. Heat pump technology has commoditized rapidly, facing severe price competition from Asian HVAC giants (Daikin, Panasonic, Midea) and diversified European heating conglomerates (Bosch, Vaillant). Historical margins and returns were inflated by a temporary, unsustainable European energy subsidy spike (2021-2023). Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC has collapsed to 6-8%, falling far short of the 12% Munger hurdle. Lack of structural pricing power demonstrated by severe margin compression (EBIT margin halved from 15% to 8% in 2024) and inventory write-downs when subsidies waned.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, lack of pricing power). European heat pump demand proved heavily subsidy-dependent, collapsing as gas prices normalized and governments rolled back incentives. NIBE lacks structural pricing power against global Asian scale leaders (Daikin, Panasonic) and diversified European majors (Bosch, Vaillant). Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC compressed to 6-8%, failing the 12% Munger moat proof standard. Waterfall terminates at Gate 3.
column21: Operating margin collapsed from 14.9% in 2023 to 8.0% in 2024, with organic sales dropping -13%. Return on capital employed (ROCE) dropped to 6.8%-8.5% in 2024 and consensus multi-year ROIC tracking at 5.7%-6.2% when accounting for acquisition goodwill. Unable to maintain price or volume in the absence of government subsidies.

column14: Fails Gate 3b. While stone wool provides superior fire resistance, insulation is fundamentally an energy-intensive industrial commodity facing direct substitution from fiberglass (Owens Corning, Saint-Gobain) and polyurethane/phenolic foams (Kingspan). Customers have virtually zero switching costs between certified insulation materials. Margins and unit economics are highly volatile and heavily exposed to natural gas, coke, and electricity input costs. Furthermore, capital intensity of melting rock at 1,500°C creates high ongoing reinvestment burdens without pricing power above inflation across full economic cycles.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Moat proof & commodity substitution). Stone wool insulation is an energy-intensive industrial commodity lacking customer switching costs or toll-booth barriers. End-customers readily substitute alternative insulation materials (fiberglass, foam, wood fiber). Vulnerability to volatile fossil energy input costs (gas, electricity, coke) and heavy ongoing capital intensity required for furnace decarbonization prevent durable pricing power above inflation across the full cycle. Waterfall terminates at Gate 3.
column21: Manufacturing stone wool requires continuous melting of basalt rock at >1,500°C, exposing gross margins to extreme European energy cost volatility. High capital expenditure requirements for furnace maintenance, emissions abatement, and localized plants dilutes owner earnings. Zero customer switching costs once building specifications are met.

column14: Local manufacturing and distribution footprint creates a regional barrier due to weight-to-value transport economics in gypsum and insulation. However, cyclical exposure to new residential construction and capital intensity prevent sustained excess returns, with 5-year median GAAP ROIC hovering around 6-8%, well below the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Heavy building products and materials manufacturer benefits from local plant density and energy-efficiency renovation demand, but structural capital intensity and cyclical new-build construction limit multi-cycle GAAP ROIC to ~6-8%.
column21: Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC hovers around 6.0-7.5% (GuruFocus), well below the 12% threshold despite portfolio pruning (divesting UK distribution, expanding in construction chemicals via Chryso and GCP). Group operating margin reached 11.4% in 2024, but goodwill and capital intensity dilute overall returns on capital.

column14: Scale and prequalification advantages in mega-infrastructure, advanced tech (data centers, battery plants via Turner), and toll road concessions (Abertis). However, construction contracting is structurally characterized by competitive bidding, thin operating margins (4-5%), and project execution risks, resulting in GAAP ROIC of 3-6%, well below the 12% threshold.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Global infrastructure contractor and concessionaire (Turner, Hochtief, Abertis) has leading positions in mega-projects and data centers, but thin contracting margins (4-5%) and competitive bidding yield sub-hurdle multi-cycle GAAP ROIC (3-6%).
column21: Operating margins remain structurally thin at ~4.5-5.0%. Consolidated GAAP ROIC sits in the 3-6% range across the cycle, far below the 12% threshold. General contracting inherently lacks pricing power against public and corporate procurement.

column14: Professional design, engineering, and environmental consultancy operates as a billable-hours people business with low barriers to entry and intense competition from global peers (WSP, AECOM, Jacobs). Lacks durable pricing power, resulting in sub-hurdle multi-cycle GAAP ROIC (~7-8%) and high susceptibility to wage inflation and project cancellations.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat Archetype 'None' & ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Design and engineering consultancy is a billable-hours professional services business with low switching barriers and high wage sensitivity, generating sub-hurdle GAAP ROIC (~7-8%).
column21: Consolidated GAAP operating margin averages 6-7% and multi-cycle GAAP ROIC remains around 7-8%, below the 12% threshold. Highly fragmented competitive environment against global engineering consultancies with zero proprietary lock-in.

column14: General construction contracting with no defensible structural moat. Competitive tendering, low switching costs, and fixed-price contract risks keep operating margins paper-thin (2-3%) and multi-cycle returns on capital volatile.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat Archetype 'None' & ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Dutch civil and commercial construction contractor operates on razor-thin operating margins (2-3%) in commoditized competitive bidding with fixed-price project overruns.
column21: Adjusted EBITDA margins of ~5% translate to GAAP operating margins of 2-3%. Historical earnings have suffered periodic severe contract write-downs and restructuring losses, with multi-cycle ROIC far below the 12% threshold.

column14: Infrastructure construction and support services business operates in competitive tendering markets with low barriers to entry and thin margins (statutory group operating margin 1.5-2.5%). Lacks structural pricing power, failing the 12% GAAP ROIC hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat Archetype 'None' & ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Infrastructure contractor operates with thin 1.5-2.5% statutory operating margins in competitive bidding, lacking structural pricing power or excess returns on capital.
column21: Statutory group operating margins hover at 1.5-2.5%, with construction services targeting only 2-3% PFO margins. While the infrastructure investment portfolio provides cash yield, overall corporate GAAP ROIC fails to clear the 12% hurdle.

column14: Irreplaceable French toll motorway network (ASF, Cofiroute, Escota) and premier international concession airports (London Gatwick, Lisbon, Edinburgh). Toll tariffs are legally and contractually indexed to French inflation, providing guaranteed annual pricing power without volume loss. 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 14.83%, exceeding the 12% hurdle, with 149% FCF conversion. Primary erosion threats include French concession tax/renegotiation risk approaching 2032-2036 motorway expiries and aviation shocks.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Irreplaceable French toll motorway network and premier international airport concessions (Gatwick, Lisbon, Edinburgh). Pricing power anchored by contractual CPI toll tariff indexation, yielding 14.8% GAAP ROIC and 149% FCF conversion. Concession debt is comfortably supported with 6.3x interest coverage and €17.3B cash cushion. [5-10Y g: motorway traffic volume 1.0% + contractual toll tariff indexation 2.0% + international airport traffic 1.5% + Vinci Energies electrification 1.5% - French concession tax/renegotiation drag 0.5% + net buybacks 0.5%]

Net debt escalated to ~€3B before being rescued via a €1B rights issue and €750M hybrid bond in 2024. Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC is structurally below 5%, far below the 12% Munger bar.

column20: Fails Gate 3 (3b=N, REJECT). column14: Installed base of minerals processing flowsheet equipment creates an aftermarket service anchor, but returns have been diluted by cyclical original equipment pricing, lumpiness, and historical EPC project execution, keeping multi-cycle GAAP ROIC well below 12%.

column14: Gas turbine installed base under long-term service agreements and proprietary high-voltage grid transmission technology provide sticky switching barriers; however, the business has been severely burdened by quality defect liabilities in Siemens Gamesa wind turbines, fixed-price project exposure, and government guarantee dependencies.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Long-cycle wind turbine and heavy energy equipment purchase trap. column21: Operating history reflects extreme cyclicality and execution volatility: FY2022 EBIT of -EUR 456M and NI of -EUR 467M; FY2023 EBIT of -EUR 3,098M and NI of -EUR 4,532M driven by massive Siemens Gamesa quality defects and warranty provisions. column14: Turbine certification and installed base service contracts offer modest continuity, but wind turbine manufacturing is a commoditized, capital-intensive business subject to fierce auction bidding, cost inflation, and aggressive Chinese OEM competition. 5-year median ROIC is negative with cumulative net losses exceeding EUR 1.1B between 2020-2023.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power). Nordex is a commoditized wind turbine manufacturer lacking economic moat or through-cycle pricing power. column21: Financial performance across the 2020-2024 cycle shows negative returns on capital and persistent operating losses: Net Loss of EUR -129.7M (2020), EUR -230.2M (2021), EUR -497.8M (2022), EUR -302.8M (2023), and a marginal Net Income of EUR 8.8M in 2024. While critical valves have high switching costs, IMI's largest division (Process Automation, >40% of sales) faces an active terminal headwind under Macrotrend [4] (Energy Transition & Resource Limits) due to heavy exposure to upstream oil & gas, petrochemicals, and thermal power.
column21: Process Automation generates ~£900m of IMI's £2.2B revenue, serving upstream hydrocarbon extraction, LNG, and conventional power generation. Decarbonization and energy transition create multi-decade demand headwinds and stranded asset risk for conventional thermal power and fossil process valves, capping CAP at 10 years.

column14: Global leader in high-pressure plunger pumps and power take-offs with ~50% market shares and 22-24% EBITDA margins.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). World leader in high-pressure plunger pumps, but 75% of sales derive from cyclical hydraulics where commercial vehicle electrification poses a long-term threat to traditional mechanical transmission PTOs.
column21: Interpump maintains strong EBITDA margins (22-24%) and dominant niche positions, but capital intensity in hydraulics and goodwill from 40+ acquisitions depress GAAP ROIC toward 9-11%. Commercial vehicle powertrain transition away from diesel engines creates terminal runway friction.

[5-10Y g: rail system deliveries 3.0% + commercial vehicle braking 2.0% + aftermarket service annuity 2.0% + pricing/margin expansion 1.0% + buybacks 0.5%]
column21: 47%+ 5-year median GAAP ROIC, operating ROIC >100%, and multi-year FCF conversion >110%. Holds 50% global share in rail brakes and 23% in commercial vehicle brakes. Net cash balance sheet with €1.7B+ in cash and zero long-term debt.

column14: Dense industrial crane service network generates stable 20%+ EBITA margins, but group returns are heavily diluted by cyclical crane equipment manufacturing and lumpy, competitive port container handling contracts.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% across cycle, REJECT). While its crane maintenance service agreement base is highly profitable, the majority of revenue derives from cyclical industrial cranes and lumpy port solutions where multi-cycle GAAP ROIC averaged 6-10% (troughing at 7.3% in 2022).
column21: Konecranes' long-term multi-cycle ROIC averaged 6-10% between 2016-2022 prior to the recent post-2023 supply chain backlog surge. Low-margin Port Solutions contracts, exposure to global freight trade volatility, and Asian competitors (e.g. ZPMC) dilute pricing power and group returns below the 12% Munger bar.

column14: Linde and STILL forklift dealer networks offer service switching costs, but group capital returns are permanently diluted by capital-intensive warehouse automation (Dematic) project volatility and rising low-cost Chinese competition.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% across cycle, REJECT). Long-term ROCE/ROIC consistently hovers in the 7-9% range (7.7% in 2025, 8.7% in 2024), failing the Munger 12% threshold due to Dematic project margin volatility and intensifying low-cost Chinese forklift competition.
column21: KION Group's 10-year average ROCE is ~7-8%, well below the cost of capital. The 2016 debt-financed acquisition of Dematic added goodwill and volatile fixed-price contract risks, while Chinese manufacturers (Hangcha, Heli) pressure new forklift pricing.

column14: Global vertical transit oligopoly with an installed base of 1.8M units. Safety regulations, proprietary elevator controls, and dense technician routes create enormous switching costs, enabling consistent inflation-plus pricing on service annuities.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Premier global elevator and escalator maintenance monopoly with 1.8M installed units under service, negative working capital, net cash fortress balance sheet, and 38% ROIC. [5-10Y g: maintenance base volume 3.5% + service contract pricing 2.0% + modernization surge 2.5% - China new equipment drag 1.0% + bolt-on M&A 0.5%]
column21: 38% 5-year median GAAP ROIC, operating ROIC >100%, and 100%+ multi-year FCF conversion. Maintenance service (+7.6%) and Modernization (+17.4%) drive high-margin recurring growth, offsetting Chinese new equipment slowdown. Long-term controlling ownership by the Herlin family.

column14: Dominates commercial combi-steamers with 50% global market share and 25%+ EBIT margins. Proprietary cooking algorithms and high energy/labor savings give customers massive ROI, supporting premium pricing without volume attrition.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Undisputed 50% global market share monopoly in commercial combi-steamer cooking appliances with zero debt, 38% ROIC, and massive customer surplus. [5-10Y g: commercial kitchen combi-steamer unit growth 4.0% + iVario/iHexagon penetration 2.5% + value-pricing power 1.5% - macro capex friction 0.5%]
column21: 38% 5-year median GAAP ROIC, 25%+ EBIT margins, and >90% FCF conversion over multiple decades. Zero structural debt with €170M+ net cash. Meister family retains controlling ownership (~55-63%). Rational appliances save kitchens up to 70% energy and 50% labor.

column14: Safety-critical valve actuators and flow control equipment embedded in customer Approved Vendor Lists (AVLs); high switching costs and >24% recurring service revenue support 30%+ ROCE and >20% operating margins.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). While Rotork is a high-return niche leader in actuators with >30% ROCE, ~45% of group revenue remains tied to Oil & Gas midstream and upstream capex. Macrotrend 4 (Energy Transition) poses an active long-term terminal headwind to fossil fuel pipeline and extraction infrastructure, capping competitive advantage period at 10 years.
column21: FY2025 revenue £777.3m, with Oil & Gas at £351m (45%), Water & Power at £223m (29%), and CPI at £203m (26%). ROCE was 38.4% in FY2025 (37.3% in FY2024), adjusted operating margin 24.6%, cash conversion 101%, with £125m+ net cash. High capital efficiency, but secular terminal headwinds on 45% oil/gas exposure limit CAP.

column20: Fails Gate 1 (Understandability / Established Operating Record, REJECT). Rosebank Industries is a newly formed (July 2024 IPO) acquisition vehicle executing a private-equity style 'Buy, Improve, Sell' turnaround strategy. It completely lacks a multi-cycle public operating track record and an established organic compounding engine.
column21: Founded by former Melrose executives, Rosebank listed as an AIM cash shell in July 2024 before graduating to the Main Market after acquiring North American electrical/industrial assets (ECI, CPM). Lacks multi-cycle consolidated operating history, recurring cash flow visibility, and organic track record as an independent operating company.

column14: Global duopoly in underground hard-rock mining equipment (with Epiroc) and market leader in cemented carbide metal cutting tools (Sandvik Coromant). Extreme switching costs from proprietary mining automation platforms (AutoMine) and mission-critical tooling consumables where cutting tool cost is <3% of workpiece value. Proven pricing power evidenced by >30% tangible ROIC and 13%+ GAAP ROIC across cycles.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in underground mining automation and precision metal-cutting tools with conservative leverage (1.5x net debt/NI), 13%+ GAAP ROIC (31%+ tangible ROIC), and 94% FCF conversion. Active beneficiary of critical minerals extraction and manufacturing automation. [5-10Y g: mining equipment/automation volume 3.5% + tooling consumable pricing 2.0% + digital manufacturing software 1.0% + net buyback 0.5%]
column21: FY2025 revenue of SEK 120.7B and EBIT of SEK 21.3B (17.6% operating margin). 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 13.1% and operating tangible ROIC is 31.4%. Owner FCF conversion averaged 94.5% (FY2025 FCF SEK 15.4B vs NI SEK 14.7B). Net debt of SEK 22.7B is repayable in 1.5 years of Owner Earnings, and interest coverage is robust at 11.7x. Spinoff of Alleima in 2022 focused the business on high-margin mining automation, rock processing, and tooling consumables.

column14: Global oligopoly in elevators and escalators with over 1.5 million units in maintenance portfolio. High switching costs and regulatory safety mandates drive recurring maintenance and modernization (>60% of revenue). column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global elevator and escalator oligopolist with over 1.5 million units in its maintenance portfolio. [5-10Y g: maintenance portfolio units 4.0% + service price escalation 2.0% + modernization 1.5% - new installation slowdown 0.5%]
column21: FY2025 revenue of CHF 10.95B and EBIT of CHF 1.40B (12.8% operating margin). 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 41.5% (tangible operating ROIC ~98%). High-margin recurring maintenance and modernizations buffer the business against China new installation headwinds.

column20: Fails Gate 3b (Sub-hurdle ROIC / Moat Proof, REJECT). SFS Group's post-Hoffmann acquisition return on invested capital has compressed to 8.4% (FY2024) and 9.3% (FY2025), failing the strict 12% ROIC moat-proof threshold. column21: FY2024 net sales CHF 3,031M, EBIT CHF 350.2M (11.6% margin), reported ROIC 8.4%. FY2025 net sales CHF 3,045M, reported EBIT CHF 324.3M (10.6% margin, 12.2% adjusted), reported ROIC 9.3%. Distribution & Logistics (Hoffmann) represents ~44% of group sales, permanently diluting group capital returns below the 12% hurdle.

column14: Global market leader in rolling bearings and condition monitoring with extensive industrial distribution networks and OEM engineering integration. Sustains ~14-15% ROCE in core industrial operations.

While SKF holds a global leading market share in rolling bearings with an established industrial distributor network, rolling bearings are increasingly standardized and face intense structural price pressure from low-cost Asian manufacturers. Furthermore, vehicle electrification reduces rotating bearing counts by 30-40%, capping its competitive advantage period well below the 15-year hurdle.
column21: FY2024 sales MSEK 98,722 with 10.5% reported operating margin; FY2025 sales MSEK 91,583 with 8.5% reported margin and net profit dropping to MSEK 4,249. Automotive separation (SKF Vertevo) highlights poor structural automotive returns (2.6-4.5% margins). Net debt MSEK 12,052. Standardized product profile and commoditization risks limit compounding runway.

column14: Outstanding pricing power: steam specialty valves, traps, and electric thermal solutions represent a tiny fraction of total plant capex but prevent catastrophic boiling/downtime; Watson-Marlow peristaltic pumps and single-use tubing are validated directly into regulated biopharmaceutical drug production filings with massive customer switching barriers.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global industrial steam thermal management and biopharma peristaltic fluid path leader. Direct engineering sales force creates exceptional switching barriers and pricing power above inflation. Net debt repayable in ~2.0 years with strong FCF conversion. [5-10Y g: steam thermal efficiency volume 2.5% + Watson-Marlow biopharma recovery 2.5% + pricing power 1.5% - debt paydown 0.5%]
column21: 14.0% 5-year median GAAP ROIC; 40-65% operating tangible ROIC. Owner FCF conversion >100% (£221.8M Owner FCF vs £163.4M NI in FY25). Watson-Marlow and Steam Thermal Solutions deliver resilient gross margins >50% across the industrial cycle.

column14: Installed base across industrial pumps, rotating equipment services, and Chemtech separation systems, but commoditized competition in flow equipment limits pricing power and leaves multi-cycle GAAP ROIC below the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Industrial pumps and flow equipment face commoditized competition from global pump manufacturers; full-cycle GAAP ROIC sits below the 12% hurdle (ROCE was 5.4% in 2022 and 9.0% in 2021) and cyclical competitive tenders restrict pricing power.
column21: Historical ROCE fluctuated between 5.4% (2022) and 9.0% (2021) before recent cyclical recovery. Competitive bidding in municipal water, oil & gas, and process industries prevents sustained pricing power above inflation.

column14: Dominant ~70% market share in reverse vending machines (RVM) and optical sorting, but powerful grocery retailers resist price increases, compressing margins during inflationary periods.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing Power, REJECT). Despite dominant reverse-vending market share, grocery retailers treat RVMs as an unwanted regulatory compliance cost and fiercely resist price increases. Operating margins collapsed from 14.2% in 2021 to 7.8% in 2023 under component and wage inflation, demonstrating lack of pricing power >= inflation.
column21: EBIT margins fell from 14.2% (2021) to 11.9% (2022) and 7.8% (2023) due to cost inflation and inability to pass prices through to grocery retail clients. Demand is subject to cyclical delays in government deposit return scheme (DRS) mandates.

column14: Niche specifications, proprietary formulations, and strict qualification testing in precision engineered polymer seals (TSS) where failure costs far exceed component prices.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Specialized engineered polymer seals operate in cyclical industrial and automotive end markets. High dependence on continuous bolt-on M&A to replace fading legacy product lines and exposure to automotive powertrain transition cap competitive advantage persistence at 10 years.
column21: Divestment of Wheel Systems in 2023 improved ROCE to 12-13% (excl. goodwill ~24%) and EBITA margins to 17-18%. However, Mauboussin capital goods base-rate persistence fades rapidly given cyclical end markets and ongoing reliance on serial bolt-on acquisitions.

column14: Installed base servicing and automation systems provide recurring revenue, but large-scale pulp, paper, and energy machinery capital projects dilute returns and lack pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Capital equipment division (~50% of revenue) involves large, lumpy, negotiated project tenders for pulp and board mills with intense competition. Multi-cycle after-tax GAAP ROIC sits at 7-10%, failing the 12% minimum hurdle.
column21: Comparable pre-tax ROCE of 12.7% (2024) and 13.0% (2025) corresponds to an after-tax ROIC of approximately 8-10%, well below the 12% threshold. Capital project orders are cyclical and subject to fierce price competition from Andritz and Voith.

column14: Global marine service and OEM parts footprint across 200+ ports; pricing power demonstrated in long-term marine lifecycle service agreements and dual-fuel engine systems, though energy storage faces fierce price competition.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Peak-to-Peak Compounding, REJECT). While marine lifecycle service agreements and OEM spare parts generate strong cash conversion and a net cash balance sheet, long-term earnings power is hostage to violent global shipbuilding and shipyard order cycles, alongside structural price competition and margin drag in grid battery energy storage.
column21: Marine and Energy operating results have historically swung with shipyard newbuild cycles (e.g. multi-year post-2008 depression in ship orders). Energy storage division operates at thin/volatile margins under heavy competition from Chinese battery integrators, undermining repeatable peak-to-peak business cycle compounding.

column11: Commodity freight price taker lacking pricing power; violent cyclicality in spot crude tanker day rates.
column20: Fails Gate 2 (Reject – G2 Essential Need). Pure-play spot crude and product tanker operator. Operates as an extreme commodity price-taker where spot day-rates fluctuate wildly based on global oil trade routes, OPEC decisions, and fleet supply cycles, resulting in boom-and-bust returns and zero durable pricing power.
column21: Frontline's fleet of VLCC, Suezmax, and LR2 tankers operates with heavy spot exposure. Historical ROIC swings between near-zero/negative in prolonged tanker recessions to transient spikes (>25%) during geopolitical rerouting bottlenecks (e.g. Red Sea and Russian crude sanctions). The company possesses no economic moat or pricing power over charterers, who select tonnage on spot market freight rates.

column14: Global scale in ocean container shipping and APM Terminals provides network density, but newbuild vessel supply across global carrier alliances repeatedly dilutes returns. 10-year average ROIC sits in the 7-9% range (well below the 12% hurdle), with extreme earnings volatility and zero durable pricing power over shippers.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Reject – G3 Moat & Pricing). Global container logistics and ocean liner giant. While operating scale and terminal infrastructure are substantial, ocean shipping is structurally commoditized and plagued by multi-year overcapacity cycles. Multi-cycle normalized ROIC of 7-9% is far below the 12% hurdle, with violent freight rate swings and lack of structural pricing power.
column21: Maersk's 10-year historical ROIC averages 7-9% (median ~7.7%), with pre-COVID 2016-2020 ROIC fluctuating around 0-4% and post-pandemic 2023-2025 ROIC cooling to 3.5-4.2% despite Red Sea re-routing. Operating earnings depend heavily on global container freight rate indices (SCFI/CCFI) and uncoordinated newbuild vessel orders across alliances, preventing consistent economic value creation.

column14: Valuable primary-airport slot portfolios at London Gatwick, Geneva, and Paris provide local frequency advantages, but short-haul aviation is structurally commoditized and shopped on OTAs. 10-year median ROIC is sub-7% (far below the 12% hurdle), with structural margin compression from volatile jet fuel, airport charges, and aggressive ULCC competition.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Reject – G3 Moat & Pricing). European low-cost passenger airline operating from primary airport slots. While Gatwick and Geneva slot portfolios offer local slot protection, easyJet's cost structure sits above ultra-low-cost peers (Ryanair/Wizz Air) while seats are commoditized. 10-year median ROIC is in the 5-7% range (failing the 12% hurdle), with zero durable pricing power over economic cycles.
column21: Over the last decade, easyJet's ROIC has averaged well below the cost of capital: 2023-2025 normalized ROIC recovered to only 4.5-8.6%, following severe pandemic losses (-10% to -12% in 2020-2021) and pre-COVID returns of 6-9% (2018-2019). High exposure to jet fuel price volatility, union wage inflation, and European passenger fare sensitivity destroys structural pricing power.

column14: Dominant slot holdings at Heathrow and Madrid provide hub-and-spoke feed advantages, but airline passenger capacity is shopped on price aggregators. Multi-cycle ROIC averages only 5-8% (failing the 12% hurdle), with volatile cash flows vulnerable to jet fuel price spikes, pilot union wage pressures, and cyclical economic downturns.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Reject – G3 Moat & Pricing). Anglo-Spanish airline group controlling British Airways and Iberia. Despite dominant slot positions at London Heathrow and Madrid-Barajas, IAG operates in a capital-intensive, cyclical industry. 10-year average ROIC lands in the 5-8% range (below the 12% hurdle), burdened by heavy fleet capex, aggressive labor unions, volatile jet fuel costs, and zero durable pricing power across full cycles.
column21: Over a full 10-year cycle, IAG's ROIC averages 5-8%, dragged down by massive pandemic-era equity dilution/losses and severe cyclical troughs, despite strong post-pandemic recovery years (17-18% in 2024-2025). The business remains a price-taker on core economy cabins, facing intense competition from low-cost carriers on short-haul and US legacy carriers on transatlantic routes, alongside high fixed aircraft lease and fuel obligations.

column14: Frankfurt and Munich hub infrastructure and Lufthansa Technik provide operational scale, but legacy cost disadvantages and unyielding union power permanently depress capital returns. 10-year average ROIC is ~2.2% (drastically failing the 12% hurdle), with constant vulnerability to pilot/ground strikes, fuel spikes, and low-cost carrier encroachment.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Reject – G3 Moat & Pricing). German flag carrier network group (Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines). While Frankfurt and Munich hub slots provide geographic density, the business is crippled by structural legacy costs and union strife. 10-year average ROIC is just ~2.2% (failing the 12% hurdle by a wide margin), with chronic labor disruption and no durable pricing power.
column21: Lufthansa's 10-year average ROIC stands at ~2.2% (15-year average 3.15%), peaking at only 7.4% in 2023 before receding to 4.2-4.4% in 2024-2025, while dipping to -7.1% during the pandemic which required a German government bailout. Operating margins are regularly wiped out by pilot, cabin crew, and ground staff strikes, soaring airport and environmental fees in Germany, and commoditized passenger fare competition.

column11: Traffic is predominantly discretionary European leisure travel; airlines are cyclical price-takers exposed to consumer spending swings and escalating EU environmental taxation.
column20: Fails Gate 2 (Reject – G2 Essential Need). Europe's leading ultra-low-cost airline. While Ryanair possesses the lowest cost per seat in Europe and an owner-operator culture, its traffic is predominantly discretionary European short-haul vacation/leisure travel, deferrable during economic downturns, and structurally exposed to consumer fare sensitivity and escalating EU environmental/carbon levies.
column21: Ryanair operates point-to-point European routes dominated by discretionary holidaymaker traffic. Despite an exceptional net-cash balance sheet (€1.3B+ net cash) and double-digit post-COVID ROIC (~17-25% in FY24-FY26), fares remain volatile and cyclical—demonstrated by 10-15% fare drops in summer 2024 when European consumers resisted higher ticket prices. As an airline, it faces structural commodity price-taker dynamics on passenger yields alongside looming ReFuelEU SAF mandates and EU ETS free allowance phase-outs.

column14: Accredited global regulatory toll booth where testing and certification costs are an insignificant fraction (<1%) of client asset value, but mandatory for operation. Global network of accredited laboratories and 190+ year reputation create high barriers to entry, enabling regular 3-4% pricing pass-through and 23%+ GAAP ROIC.

Mandatory regulatory compliance provides resilient, inflation-indexed revenue with minimal capex. Net debt 1.7x net income with 10.2x interest coverage. Sales expanded from €5,651M (2022) to €6,466M (2025) with operating margins at ~15%. Balance sheet is sound with net debt of €1,023.8M repayable in 1.7 years of net income and interest coverage of 10.18x.

AI is an operational tailwind driving data consumption. Net debt 2.8x net income with 9.6x interest coverage. Sales expanded from $6,619M (FY22) to $8,445M (FY25) with operating margins expanding to 25.8%. Net debt of $4,242M is 2.82x net income with robust interest coverage of 9.59x.

Testing fees are an insignificant fraction of product cost but legally mandatory for commerce. Net debt 2.4x net income with 11.1x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: organic volume 3.0% + pricing power 1.5% + margin expansion 0.5% + bolt-on M&A/buybacks 1.0%]
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 20.5% and operating ROIC >100%. Free cash flow conversion averages 127.7% (FY2025 Owner FCF of £367.7M vs NI of £343.5M). Revenue rose to £3,432M in FY25 with operating margin reaching 18.1% (and >30% in Consumer Products). Net debt of £833.2M is covered 2.43x by net income, and interest coverage is 11.11x.

Proved by 24.3% median GAAP ROIC, >30% operating margins, and consistent 2-4% pricing power with minimal churn.

Net debt 2.7x net income with 11.1x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: Risk/Analytics organic 4.5% + Legal/STM price and AI upsell 1.5% + margin expansion 0.5% + net share buybacks 1.5%]
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 24.3% and operating ROIC >100%. Free cash flow conversion averages 109.9% (FY2025 Owner FCF of £2,248M vs NI of £2,065M). Revenue reached £9,590M in FY25 with operating profit of £3,023M (31.5% margin). Net debt of £5,498M is 2.66x net income, and interest coverage is 11.07x.

column14: Unrivaled global physical lab and inspection footprint operating as a certified toll booth for international trade and regulatory compliance. Proved by 34.5% median GAAP ROIC, consistent 15-16% EBIT margins, and demonstrated 3-4% pricing pass-through.

Strong operational execution under Strategy '27 with expanding margins. Net debt 1.8x net income with 13.7x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: organic volume 3.5% + price pass-through 1.5% + margin expansion 0.5% + bolt-on M&A net of scrip 0.5%]

Revenue rose to CHF 6,945M in FY25 with operating profit reaching CHF 1,038M (16.0% AOI margin). Net debt of CHF 1,175M is 1.76x net income and interest coverage is 13.66x.

Leading European engineering and architectural consultancy, but operates a billable-hour professional services model characterized by competitive project bidding, low customer switching costs, and cyclical reliance on construction and public infrastructure procurement. Also faces long-term headwind from AI-assisted CAD/BIM design tools compressing billable engineering hours.

Pricing reflects labor rate inflation pass-through rather than structural economic rent extraction.

Net debt 2.3x net income and 15.1x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: recurring volume 3.5% + pricing power 2.0% + margin expansion 0.5% + net buybacks 1.0%]

Revenue grew from €5.45B (2022) to €6.13B (2025) while EBIT margin reached 28.8%. Net debt of €3,063M is covered 2.34x by net income and interest coverage is 15.1x.

GAAP ROIC of 1.6% reflects €13B+ in private equity buyout goodwill.

Bulk industrial chemical volumes are cyclical and vulnerable to European industrial weakness and chemical price deflation. Net debt stands at ~€2.5-3.0B (leverage ~2.0-2.3x EBITDA).

column20: Defensive consumables compounder with multi-decade compounding record. column21: GAAP ROIC consistently 17-22% (median 20.6%), with operating ROIC >100%. Free cash flow conversion averages >100% (FY25 Owner FCF £838M vs NI £459M). 31+ consecutive years of dividend increases. Leverage at 2.0x net debt/EBITDA (£1.2B net debt repayable in ~1.4 years of Owner FCF), comfortably weathering the temporary 2025 US foodservice margin dip.
