Mission-critical components with negligible customer cost share ensure continuous pricing power, while disciplined bolt-ons at ~6-7x EBIT drive double-digit compounding. column21: Gross margin expanded to 61.6% in 2024 and 62.7% in 2025 despite UK construction headwinds. Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC is 20-34% (median 21.1%). Zero financial bank debt (£344.5M cash balances outweigh financial debt, with reported debt comprising IFRS 16 depot leases); interest coverage >15x.

Normalization after post-COVID supply shortage windfalls resulted in organic EBITA declines and drove GAAP ROIC to 8.9% in 2025, below the 12% threshold.
column21: GAAP ROIC deteriorated from 14.5% in 2022 to 12.3% in 2024 and 8.88% in 2025. Operating EBIT fell from €463.5M in 2022 to €360.9M in 2025. Operating EBITA dropped 6% reported in 2025 amid soft industrial chemical demand, while balance sheet debt expanded to €1.29B (net debt ~€1.05B) to fund roll-up M&A.

Balance sheet maintains conservative net debt / NI of 1.58x and interest coverage of 8.3x (BBB- investment grade). Completed 13 disciplined bolt-on acquisitions in FY2025, accelerating into 2026 with Q3 EBITA margins expanding to 15.3%.

column14: Global distribution scale and high catalog availability across 750,000+ MRO and electronic products provide localized inventory convenience; historically delivered 15-20%+ ROCE, though operating margins have compressed from 12.8% to 8.0% as digital catalog competition intensifies.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Broadline catalog distribution of standardized electronic components and MRO supplies faces severe terminal headwinds from supplier digital disintermediation, specialized online distributors (Digi-Key, Mouser), and horizontal platforms (Amazon Business). Compressed operating margins (falling from 12.8% in FY23 to 8.0% in FY25) reflect structural margin fade and limited long-term pricing defense.
column21: Statutory operating margins compressed from 12.8% in FY23 to 10.6% in FY24 and 8.0% in FY25 (adjusted 9.4%). ROCE fell from 29.7% in FY23 to 15.2% in FY25 amid sluggish industrial volumes and increased pricing transparency. Lack of proprietary products or engineer-embedded IP leaves RS Group vulnerable to digital disintermediation and platform aggregation over a 15-year horizon.

column14: Extensive branch network and logistics scale across North America and Europe provide distributor availability, but lack structural pricing power; margins are thin (~5.9-6.8% EBITA) and heavily exposed to copper cable pricing cycles, while multi-cycle GAAP ROIC (~5-8%) falls well below the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (N, REJECT). Global electrical wholesale distributor benefiting from electrification trends, but lacks structural pricing power and fails Gate 3b. Operating profitability is constrained by thin ~6% EBITA margins, heavy sensitivity to copper commodity cycles and manufacturer rebates (Schneider, ABB, Legrand), and sub-hurdle multi-cycle GAAP ROIC of 5-8% (well below the 12% threshold). Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
column21: Reported adjusted EBITA margins of 6.8% (2023), 5.9% (2024), and 6.0% (2025). Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC historically tracks between 4.5% and 8.0%, failing the 12% quality hurdle. Gross margins are structurally exposed to copper raw material pass-through timing differences and supplier volume rebates rather than independent customer pricing power.

column14: European scale in steel and materials distribution provides logistics reach, but zero pricing power; operating margins are razor-thin (~2-2.8% EBITDA, ~1% EBIT) and multi-cycle returns on capital fall far short of the 12% ROIC threshold.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (N, REJECT). Spun off from thyssenkrupp in October 2026, tk accelis is a commodity materials distributor and steel service center operating with razor-thin ~2-2.8% adjusted EBITDA margins (~1% EBIT). Lacks structural pricing power as a pure price-taker in cyclical steel and industrial metals, generating sub-hurdle multi-cycle returns on capital well below the 12% ROIC requirement. Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
column21: FY2024/25 sales of €11.4B generated an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 2%, rising modestly to 2.8% in the first 9 months of FY25/26 (€256M EBITDA on €9.1B revenue). Structural EBIT margins hover near 1%, and ROCE/ROIC is in the low-to-mid single digits, failing the 12% hurdle. High working capital intensity and commodity inventory price risk prevent sustainable excess economic returns.

column14: Deep CAD/PLM standard lock-in across global aerospace, defense, and automotive engineering lifecycles (CATIA, SOLIDWORKS, ENOVIA) creates multi-decade customer switching barriers; demonstrated by 17.2% median GAAP ROIC, >32% operating margins, and pricing power exceeding inflation.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global industrial standard in 3D CAD/PLM software (CATIA, SOLIDWORKS, 3DEXPERIENCE) with unassailable switching barriers in aerospace and automotive engineering, generating >114% FCF conversion and backed by a €2.98B net cash balance sheet fortress. [5-10Y g: organic cloud/PLM volume 4.0% + price 2.0% + mix/reinvestment 0.5% - auto cyclical drag 0.5% + net buyback 0.5%]
column21: Reported 4-year median GAAP ROIC of 17.16% (tangible ROIC >100%). Cumulative 4-year Owner FCF of €5,032M on Net Income of €4,379M delivers 114.9% cash conversion. Balance sheet holds €4,125M in cash against €1,146M in long-term debt (€2,979.6M net cash) with 35.6x interest coverage. While Life Sciences (Medidata) faced transitional headwinds in FY25 (4% revenue growth), core industrial engineering software retains high renewal rates and expanding subscription ARR.

column14: Deep contractor and architect workflow integration via Bluebeam and Archicad standards; switching costs and file compatibility create formidable moats, enabling double-digit ARR expansion across the SaaS transition with negligible churn and a 29.1% median GAAP ROIC.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Premier AEC/O software provider with dominant positions in construction workflow (Bluebeam) and European BIM (Archicad, Allplan); successfully transformed into a recurring SaaS engine with >150% multi-year FCF conversion and negligible leverage. [5-10Y g: organic AEC/cloud volume 6.0% + price 2.5% + mix/reinvestment 1.0% - construction cyclical drag 0.5% + net buyback 0.0%]
column21: Reported 4-year median GAAP ROIC of 29.11% (tangible ROIC >100%). Cumulative 4-year Owner FCF of €1,117.3M on GAAP Net Income of €715.8M yields 156.1% FCF conversion. Net debt / NI stands at an ultra-low 0.49x (€107.5M net debt vs €217.2M net income) with 16.0x EBIT interest coverage. FY2025 revenue surged 22.6% to €1,191.2M with subscription/SaaS ARR exceeding €1.19B (€1.46B by Q3 2026), demonstrating elite execution and pricing resilience.

column14: Mission-critical plant lifecycle and engineering software is sticky once embedded, but pricing power is unproven on a standalone basis outside Hexagon's hardware bundles, and it lacks an audited multi-year standalone ROIC track record while carrying legacy heavy R&D capitalization.

column21: Spun off from Hexagon AB in 2026. Lacks standalone 5-year public financial history to verify median GAAP ROIC >= 12% and owner FCF conversion under standalone cost structure. High historical software capitalization raises uncertainty on true economic returns.

column14: Prohibitive ERP replacement pain and deeply embedded workflow integrations provide immense lock-in, enabling regular 3-5% maintenance price increases and 20-30%+ contract value uplifts on cloud migrations.

[5-10Y g: organic cloud/RISE migration 5.0% + pricing/contract uplifts 2.0% + operating leverage 1.0% + net buyback 1.0%]
column21: Tangible ROIC consistently 40%-200% (operating ROIC 84.4%), GAAP ROIC reaching 18.8% in FY25. Cash of €8.2B exceeds LT debt of €4.2B with interest coverage >21x. Over 85% of Global 2000 rely on SAP as mission-critical digital core.

column14: High switching costs in core accounting and payroll ledgers for SMBs and mid-market enterprises, supported by regulatory compliance mandates; proved by 4-6% annual price hikes and 100%+ net retention.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Essential accounting and payroll ledger for SMBs and mid-market enterprises benefiting from compliance lock-in and high recurring cash conversion. Net debt easily serviceable. [5-10Y g: organic Sage Intacct / cloud volume 4.5% + pricing 2.5% + margin expansion 0.5% + net share repurchases 1.5%]
column21: Multi-year median GAAP ROIC of 17.4% (reaching 23.2% in FY25) with >100% tangible ROIC. Owner FCF conversion averages 114%. Net debt / NI of 2.94x and interest coverage of 9.8x provide comfortable solvency.

column14: Installed core banking software is sticky once deployed, but new win rates have decelerated, bespoke bank RFPs compress margins and pricing power, and aggressive R&D capitalization obscures underlying economic returns.

While installed core banking software has high switching costs, new license win rates have stalled, banks exert heavy pricing pressure in bespoke RFPs, and aggressive R&D capitalization masks sub-hurdle true cash returns amidst competition from cloud-native fintech engines.
column21: Loss of market momentum in core banking migrations to cloud-native rivals (Thought Machine, Mambu). Substantial license earnings volatility, governance turnover, and reliance on R&D capitalization to sustain reported operating margins.

Multi-cycle ROIC falls well short of the 12% hurdle, burdened by cyclical operator capex declines and destructive M&A write-downs (SEK 43B+ Vonage impairment).
column21: Sub-12% multi-cycle GAAP ROIC, lack of pricing power against major wireless carriers, and massive capital destruction from the $6.2B Vonage acquisition resulting in over SEK 43B in goodwill impairments.

column14: Strong cellular standard essential patent portfolio and optical network tech, but core Mobile Networks faces commoditized pricing, customer concentration, and intense competition from Ericsson.

While Nokia possesses high-quality patent licensing and optical transport assets, its core Mobile Networks division suffers from chronic sub-12% multi-cycle ROIC, commoditized pricing pressure, and customer vulnerability as evidenced by losing AT&T's multi-billion dollar RAN contract to Ericsson.
column21: Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC consistently below the 12% threshold (hovering in mid-single digits). Continuous restructuring charges, price deflation in mobile RAN hardware, and customer concentration risk (loss of AT&T footprint).

column14: High gross margins (~66%) and proprietary Leica calibration/metrology software workflows create substantial switching costs, enabling above-inflation pricing across cycles.

Strong Leica Geosystems and industrial metrology franchises, but decades of debt/equity-funded M&A rollups have bloated invested capital with >€12B of goodwill, driving sub-hurdle GAAP ROIC (8.2%) and sluggish peak-to-peak Owner EPS compounding (0.5% CAGR).
column21: Reported GAAP ROIC median of 8.21% (2022: 8.4%, 2023: 8.0%, 2024: 9.0%, 2025: 5.8%). Goodwill and intangibles of €12.1B exceed total equity of €10.2B, leaving negative tangible equity. Net income fell from €1,023M in 2024 to €617M in 2025. 4-year Owner EPS CAGR is only 0.53% (peak 0.378 in 2024 falling to 0.293 in 2025). High gross margins (66%) and healthy FCF conversion (95.6%) are insufficient to overcome structurally dilutive acquisition accounting and industrial cyclicality.

column14: Low-ticket, high-liability, regulation-mandated safety and medical devices (>60% gross margin) consistently pass through above-inflation price increases while maintaining ~20% EBIT margins.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Archetypal UK decentralized compounder in regulation-mandated safety, environmental, and medical niches with self-funded bolt-on M&A and minimal disruption risk. [5-10Y g: organic volume 4.5% + price 1.5% + self-funded bolt-on M&A 3.5%]
column21: Median GAAP ROIC of 13.62% with operating ROIC of 61.05%. FCF conversion exceeds 112% (FY2025 Owner FCF £392.4M vs Net Income £372.3M). 4-year Owner EPS compounded at 14.2% CAGR from £0.765 to £1.140. Net debt of £613.3M is easily covered by Owner Earnings (Net Debt / NI = 1.65x), and EBIT/Interest coverage is 15.1x. Exceptional capital allocation record with 45+ consecutive years of >=5% dividend growth.

column14: Niche sensor know-how, vacuum measurement IP, and OEM design-ins into semiconductor fabrication equipment create high switching costs and robust pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Niche leader in vacuum gauges and leak detection, but semicap capital equipment cyclicality combined with severe geopolitical/trade embargo risk (>30% China revenue exposure) limits predictable competitive advantage period.
column21: INFICON maintains strong operating margins (~17-20%) and high ROIC on low tangible capital, but >30% of sales are tied directly to China semiconductor customers amidst intensifying Western export controls and aggressive Chinese domestic substitution. Severe semicap cyclicality and OEM gatekeepers truncate the competitive advantage runway well below the 15-year threshold.

column14: Process know-how and qualification in high-end IC substrates and PCBs, but structurally lacks pricing power against dominant semi customers.

column21: Depressed multi-cycle GAAP ROIC (<6% median) and extreme margin volatility. Capex-heavy manufacturing model with massive debt-funded capacity expansions in Kulim, Malaysia and Leoben, Austria. Customer power is overwhelmingly concentrated among a few dominant semi giants (AMD, Intel, Apple), leaving AT&S as a price-taker unable to earn its cost of capital across the cycle.

Billable-hour IT consulting and services model faces persistent margin pressure from client cost-takeout mandates and generative AI delivery deflation, with sub-12% multi-cycle GAAP ROIC following large goodwill acquisitions (Altran, WNS).
column21: 5-year GAAP ROIC remains structurally sub-hurdle (~9-11%) due to €10B+ in goodwill and intangibles from serial M&A (Altran, WNS, Cloud4C). Operating margins are capped at ~13%. Labour-intensive consulting and IT services lack pricing power above inflation as enterprise clients routinely enforce productivity clawbacks, a headwind accelerating under AI automation.

column14: Network of specialized digital consultancies with high talent retention, but lacks proprietary software IP or locked-in toll booths. Margins are capped at ~14% EBIT and day rates face intense procurement competition and AI coding automation deflation.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Italian IT consulting network with solid organic execution, but operates as a talent-dependent service provider selling billable hours without proprietary software lock-in or pricing power above wage inflation. Highly vulnerable to corporate procurement pressure and AI software development deflation.
column21: Revenue grew from €1,250.2M (2020) to €2,300.5M (2024), with EBIT margins stable between 13.6% and 15.1% (€330.4M EBIT in 2024). Net cash position reached €349.1M at year-end 2024. While reported ROIC appears high at ~20-24% due to an asset-light consulting balance sheet, Reply lacks structural switching costs or pricing power: clients regularly tender IT integration projects via competitive corporate RFPs. The service model faces structural margin compression as AI coding agents commoditize routine digital services.

column14: Embedded relationships in French public sector and defense, but sub-hurdle capital efficiency (RoCE 6.7-7.5% vs 12% hurdle) and single-digit operating margins (7-9%) prove lack of an economic moat. Highly vulnerable to IT services commoditization and public sector budget austerity.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Undifferentiated French IT services provider with sub-hurdle capital efficiency (RoCE 6.7-7.5% vs 12% requirement) and thin operating margins (~8%). Heavy reliance on price-sensitive French public-sector RFPs leaves zero pricing power above inflation.
column21: Operating margin on business activity was 8.1% (2021), 8.9% (2022), 9.4% (2023), and 9.8% (2024), with standard reported operating margins of 7.5%-8.9%. Reported RoCE was 6.7% in 2021 and 7.5% in 2022, structurally failing the 12% ROIC threshold. Growth has been heavily reliant on M&A rollups (CS Group, Ordina) while core organic growth is sluggish. Public-sector customer concentration exposes the business to sovereign procurement spending freezes and billable-hour deflation from AI tooling.

column14: Specialized MOCVD process know-how for GaN and SiC deposition, but lacks through-cycle economic moat proof: highly cyclical lumpy tool orders, volatile ROIC dropping to 11.5% in 2024 (and negative in 2015-2016), heavy customer concentration in Asia, and high export regulation risk.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Niche MOCVD equipment maker subject to violent boom-bust cycles in compound semiconductor (GaN/SiC) capex. Severe order volatility, ROIC dropping to ~11.5% in 2024 (and multi-year operating losses in past downturns), and concentrated Chinese customer exposure demonstrate lack of through-cycle pricing power.
column21: Revenue rose from €429M (2021) to €633M (2024), but historical track record reveals severe earnings volatility: EBIT was -€26.7M in 2015, -€21.4M in 2016, and +€4.9M in 2017. While ROIC peaked at ~25.7% during the 2021-2022 EV/SiC capex boom, it fell to ~11.5% in 2024 as power semi fab capacity saturated. Tools are lumpy one-off capital purchases that customers easily defer in downturns, with heavy revenue concentration in Asian foundries subject to geopolitical export licensing barriers.

column14: Process-of-record qualification 3-5 years ahead of fab ramp creates insurmountable switching costs for foundries (TSMC, Intel, Samsung). Gross margin expanded from 47% to 51% over the cycle, with GAAP ROIC consistently 25-30% and tangible ROIC >40%. Primary risks: customer concentration among top 3 foundries and US/EU export restrictions on shipments to China.

Irreplaceable fab recipe lock-in with >50% market share and 25%+ GAAP ROIC. Net cash fortress exceeding €1B with zero long-term debt. [5-10Y g: wafer fab & GAA/ALD intensity 8.5% + price/mix 1.5% + margin 0.5% + buybacks 0.5%]
column21: Multi-year GAAP ROIC averaged 25.0% (operating tangible ROIC 42.5%). Gross margin expanded from 47% to 51% over the cycle. Revenue grew from €2,410.9M in 2022 to €3,173.2M in 2025, while EBIT grew from €506.5M to €925.8M. Cash conversion is outstanding with Owner FCF of €762.2M in 2025 on Net Income of €723.7M (105% conversion; multi-year FCF conversion 91.3%). Balance sheet is a fortress with €1,026.8M in cash and €0 long-term debt (interest coverage >1000x). ASM is the Process-of-Record (POR) ALD supplier for TSMC, Intel, and Samsung on Gate-All-Around (GAA) logic nodes, creating massive technological switching barriers.

column14: Global monopoly on extreme ultraviolet (EUV) photolithography protected by proprietary optics (Zeiss exclusive partnership), laser-produced plasma source IP, and thousands of patents. Extraordinary pricing power demonstrated by EUV tool ASPs scaling from €120M to >€350M for High-NA while maintaining >51% gross margins and ~98% median GAAP ROIC. Primary risks: geopolitical export curbs on shipments to China and customer concentration (TSMC, Samsung, Intel).
column20: Unassailable global commercial monopoly on EUV lithography machines essential for all leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing. Unprecedented pricing power with tool ASPs climbing from €120M to >€350M for High-NA tools and 98%+ median GAAP ROIC. Sovereign semiconductor reshoring and AI computing act as massive secular catalysts. Fortress balance sheet with >€10B net cash. [5-10Y g: litho wafer demand & EUV/High-NA intensity 8.0% + tool ASP/service mix 2.0% + margin 0.5% + buybacks 1.0%]
column21: Multi-year median GAAP ROIC is 98.6% (operating tangible ROIC >150%). Gross margin has consistently maintained 51-53% and EBIT margins ~35%. Revenue expanded from €21.17B in 2022 to €32.67B in 2025, with Owner EPS reaching a record peak of €24.71 in 2025. Owner FCF was €11.43B in 2025 (119% conversion of Net Income; multi-year FCF conversion 110.7%). Balance sheet holds €12.92B in cash against €2.71B in long-term debt (net cash of €10.21B), with interest coverage of ~97x. Monopolistic market share in EUV with multi-year backlog and ~25% high-margin installed base recurring service revenue.

column14: Industry-leading ~64-65% gross margins and >35% operating margins demonstrate strong pricing power and engineering lock-in for high-precision die attach and hybrid bonding equipment used in chiplet and HBM packaging.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Compounding Stability & Balance Sheet, REJECT). World-class ~65% gross margins and hybrid-bonding leadership for 2.5D/3D chiplets and HBM, but extreme backend packaging capex cyclicality (>37% net income drop from 2021 peak to 2023-2024) and reliance on convertible note issuances to fund aggressive capital distributions violate Gate 6 fortress peace of mind.
column21: Revenue fell from €749.3M (2021) to €578.9M (2023) before recovering slightly to €607.5M (2024). Net income dropped >37% from €282.4M in 2021 to €177.1M in 2023 and €182.0M in 2024, demonstrating severe backend assembly capex cyclicality. While gross margins are elite at ~64-65% and FCF conversion is high (~€189M FCF in 2024), management aggressively leverages capital returns via convertible debt and senior notes (€350M issued in 2024), causing cash to swing from €671.7M down to €413.5M in 2023 following €435.5M in distributions.

column14: Specialized RF plasma control impedance matching and microfocus X-ray inspection modules embedded in semiconductor fab equipment. While switching costs exist during a tool design cycle, extreme customer concentration (monopsonistic semicap OEMs like Lam Research and Applied Materials) strips Comet of structural pricing power, subjecting returns to severe downcycle margin compression.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC/pricing power, REJECT). Specialized supplier of RF plasma control modules and X-ray systems to semiconductor equipment OEMs. Severe customer concentration (Lam Research, AMAT) and intense semicap capex cyclicality strip Comet of independent pricing power, causing ROCE to collapse from 26% in 2021-2022 to 6.6% in 2023.
column21: Comet Holding AG supplies RF power delivery systems and X-ray inspection modules. Operating profitability is acutely exposed to the wafer fab equipment (WFE) capex cycle. Consolidated OEM buyers hold superior negotiating leverage. ROCE dropped sharply from 26.8% (2021) and 26.3% (2022) to 6.6% (2023) and 10.4% (2024), demonstrating sub-hurdle trough returns and absence of cycle-neutral pricing power.

column14: Undisputed near-monopoly (>90% global market share) in advanced display photomask laser pattern generators (Prexision series), supplemented by semiconductor photomask writers (SLX) and SMT PCB assembly solutions. Extreme optical precision IP, customer workflow lock-in, and lucrative recurring maintenance service contracts drive 34%+ median GAAP ROIC and >50% gross margins.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global monopoly in flat-panel display photomask writers with expanding footprint in semiconductor mask writing and SMT electronics assembly. Exceptional capital efficiency (median ROIC 34%), >100% FCF conversion, and net cash fortress balance sheet (SEK 2.3B net cash). [5-10Y g: mask-writer & SMT equipment volume 4.5% + price/mix 1.5% + bolt-on acquisitions 1.0% - tax/capex normalization drag 0.5% + capital return 0.5%]
column21: Mycronic generates SEK 7.9B in revenue with 25% EBIT margins. In display photomask pattern generation, it has essentially zero commercial competition for advanced OLED/AMOLED screens. 4-year financial history shows median GAAP ROIC of 34.4%, operating ROIC >100%, and multi-year FCF/NI conversion of 100.5%. The balance sheet is a fortress with SEK 2.32B cash against SEK 12M long-term debt, providing complete immunity from credit markets.

column14: Patented Smart Cut wafer splitting technology provides engineering differentiation in RF-SOI and FD-SOI engineered substrates. However, customer concentration among a few foundries and fabless RF designers, combined with heavy fab capex requirements and rapid Chinese substrate overcapacity (notably in SiC), prevents structural pricing power above inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC/pricing power, REJECT). Proprietary Smart Cut substrate IP is compromised by heavy capital expenditure intensity (€230M annual capex vs €91M FY25 net income), pronounced inventory cyclicality in smartphone RF chips, and rapid price erosion in Silicon Carbide substrates from expanding Chinese domestic capacity.
column21: Soitec's financial track record exhibits severe cyclicality and poor cash conversion. Net income dropped by 60% from €231.9M in FY23 to €91.2M in FY25, while annual capex absorbed €230M, leaving negligible free cash flow. Monopsonistic foundry customers (TSMC, GlobalFoundries) and aggressive price deflation in power electronics wide-bandgap substrates limit cycle-neutral pricing power and compress multi-cycle ROIC.

column14: Advanced MEMS and vertical probe cards feature proprietary micro-fabrication IP and tight engineering integration with leading chip designers. However, probe cards are custom-engineered per chip tape-out and subject to constant dual-sourcing bake-offs against FormFactor and Asian competitors. Concentrated customers (foundries, integrated device manufacturers) exert strong pricing leverage, compressing operating margins by ~17-18 percentage points between 2022 and 2025.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (pricing power/proof of moat, REJECT). World-class MEMS probe card manufacturer faces intense head-to-head dual-sourcing re-bidding against FormFactor and Asian competitors for each chip tape-out. Concentrated semiconductor buyers exercise strong purchasing power, causing EBIT margins to compress by ~17-18 percentage points (from 37.8% in 2022 to 20.5% in 2025) and preventing peak-to-peak EPS compounding.
column21: Technoprobe's revenues grew from €548.9M in FY22 to €628.4M in FY25, yet EBIT fell 38% from €207.4M to €129.0M, and Net Income plunged from €147.9M to €97.7M (Owner EPS dropped from €0.25 to €0.15). Operating margins experienced severe structural dilution (from 37.8% down to 20.5%) driven by mix shifts, DIS integration, and customer pricing pressure across competitive node transitions, failing the Munger standard for cycle-neutral pricing power.

column14: Unassailable ~71% global market share in semiconductor vacuum valves. Valves represent <1% of wafer fabrication equipment cost but are mission-critical (valve failure destroys entire wafer runs), creating extreme spec-in switching costs for semicap OEMs (ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research). Consistently defends 30-35% EBITDA margins and >26% GAAP ROIC across semiconductor cycles despite Swiss franc strength.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global monopoly (~71% share) in mission-critical vacuum valves for semiconductor manufacturing. Beneficiary of AI-driven node transitions (increasing vacuum process steps) and global fab reshoring. Pristine net cash balance sheet, >99% multi-year FCF conversion, and industry-leading returns on capital. [5-10Y g: semicap vacuum valve & service volume 6.5% + price/spec-in mix 1.5% + margin expansion 0.5% + capital return 0.5%]
column21: VAT Group commands ~71% global market share in semiconductor vacuum valves with over 3x the share of its nearest competitor. 4-year financial data confirms median GAAP ROIC of 27.8%, operating ROIC >70%, and multi-year Owner FCF conversion of 99.2%. Intra-cycle EPS moderation in 2023-2025 reflects normal WFE digestion rather than moat erosion. Balance sheet is in a net cash position (CHF 141M cash vs CHF 45M LT debt) with interest coverage >70x.

column14: Global market leader in automotive microcontrollers (AURIX) and power semiconductors (IGBTs, SiC, GaN) with high switching barriers due to automotive safety qualifications (ISO 26262). However, structural pricing power above inflation is absent due to institutionalized automotive OEM annual contractual cost-down demands, heavy front-end fab capital intensity (Dresden and Kulim expansions), and aggressive Chinese state-backed capacity additions in power discretes.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC/pricing power, REJECT). Leading automotive and industrial power semiconductor IDM suffers from extreme capital intensity (multi-billion euro fab commitments), relentless OEM contractual price-down demands, and surging Chinese state-backed capacity in power discretes, causing RoCE to fall to 4.9% in FY25 and FCF to turn negative.
column21: Infineon's Group RoCE collapsed from 16.6% in FY23 to 8.5% in FY24 and 4.9% in FY25, well below the 12% compounder hurdle. Automotive Segment Result Margin dropped from ~29% in FY22 to ~16% in FY24. Free cash flow was €23M in FY24 and negative -€1,051M in FY25 under heavy fab capex outflows, while net debt expanded to ~€3.0B. Tier-1 automotive customer purchasing power and Chinese domestic substitution prevent pricing power above inflation.

column14: Entrenched developer mindshare and proprietary nRF Connect SDK create software switching costs in Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), but component pricing power against Tier-1 OEMs is limited.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Global leader in ultra-low power Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) chips with sticky developer ecosystem, but short customer product cycles, intense price competition from Chinese fabless rivals (Espressif, Telink), and high exposure to cyclical consumer IoT gadget demand cap the competitive advantage runway at 5 years.
column21: Revenues contracted from $777M in 2022 to $511M in 2024 with operating losses (-$44M in 2024) highlighting violent consumer IoT inventory destocking cycles. While historical median ROIC exceeded 15% during the 2021-2022 boom, long-term capital persistence is curtailed by continuous silicon commoditization and foundry cost inflation.

column14: Extensive STM32 microcontroller developer ecosystem and long automotive qualification cycles create design-in switching costs, but heavy internal fab capital intensity and cyclical ASP erosion prevent sustained >12% ROIC across the cycle.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Capital-intensive integrated device manufacturer (IDM) exposed to severe automotive and industrial chip downcycles, aggressive Chinese silicon carbide (SiC) capacity expansion, and customer concentration (Apple, Tesla), keeping multi-cycle ROIC below the 12% hurdle.
column21: Multi-cycle ROIC falls to low single digits (~3-5%) during downcycles, failing the 12% cycle-average hurdle. Massive annual fab capex ($2.5B-$4B) creates high operating leverage, and the lack of secular pricing power against Tier-1 automotive and consumer OEMs leads to periodic margin compression.

column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). column21: Historical GAAP ROIC tracks between 6% and 7%, well below the 12% threshold. Operating margins remain capped around 5-6% as hardware reselling and low-complexity IT provisioning face constant price competition and threat of disintermediation by direct vendor sales and cloud hyperscaler marketplaces.

column14: Volume procurement partnerships with Tier-1 OEMs (Apple, Microsoft, Cisco) and large enterprise relationships provide distribution scale, but wafer-thin operating margins (~2.5%) and commodity bidding dynamics demonstrate a lack of genuine pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). IT infrastructure and hardware reseller operating on razor-thin operating margins (~2-3%) without pricing power, subject to competitive public/corporate procurement tenders and long-term disintermediation by direct OEM sales and cloud hyperscaler marketplaces.
column21: Operating margins consistently track between 2.1% and 2.8%, reflecting commoditized pass-through technology sourcing. While capital employed is low due to customer financing terms, the underlying business is a middleman price-taker unable to increase prices above inflation without risking enterprise client defections.

column14: High-touch customer service and strong sales culture have driven UK IT reseller market share gains, but near-zero client switching costs and vendor-controlled commission structures prevent independent pricing power above inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Asset-light UK IT reseller with impressive sales execution and cash generation, but inherently lacks structural pricing power; margins are determined by vendor rebate structures (Microsoft, Cisco) and client procurement tenders with negligible switching barriers.
column21: Operating margins on Gross Invoiced Income remain tight at ~5.4-5.5%. While accounting ROCE appears high due to an asset-light balance sheet and working capital terms, the business model is an intermediary price-taker vulnerable to vendor margin squeezes and direct cloud marketplace purchasing.

The business cannot escape global aluminum supply-demand cycles and lacks unilateral pricing power above inflation.

Permitted kilns and US river terminals confer strong local scale, but bulk cement remains a cyclical, carbon-intensive commodity with 10-year average ROCE below 10% and heavy EU ETS decarbonisation capex burdens.

Free cash flow conversion is depressed at 59.3% due to high ongoing maintenance and environmental capex. The business lacks unilateral through-cycle pricing power against structural energy and carbon costs.

column14: Permitted quarries, cement kilns, and aggregate deposits provide local transport-radius advantages, but heavy capital intensity and regional commodity cement pricing dynamics keep multi-cycle returns depressed.

column21: Reported ROIC over the 2015-2024 decade ranged between 6.3% and 10.3%, failing to achieve the 12% threshold in any single year (5-year median 10.67%). Heavy capital intensity combined with cyclical pricing in bulk cement prevents through-cycle economic profits. The company faces multi-billion-euro decarbonization capex requirements under EU ETS rules.

Bulk cement economics lack through-cycle pricing power above energy and structural carbon costs. The spin-off of high-margin North American assets (Amrize) leaves the remaining entity heavily exposed to European ETS decarbonization capex.

column21: 100% of mining operations (Los Pelambres, Centinela, Antucoya, Zaldívar) are located in Chile. Revenue and cash flow swing violently with LME copper spot prices and treatment/refining charges. Mining royalties, political revisions to Chilean mining codes, and severe regional water constraints in the Atacama/Coquimbo regions present continuous operating and capital expenditure hurdles.

Deep underground domestic mines face rising extraction and labor costs, compounded by Poland's heavy copper extraction tax (podatek od wydobycia niektórych kopalin) and historic value-destructive foreign M&A (Sierra Gorda).

column14: Complex multimetal smelting and recycling infrastructure provides technological processing scale, but treatment charges (TC/RCs) and metal premia are dictated by global benchmark negotiations and Chinese smelting capacity, leaving Aurubis as a margin taker without pricing power.

Aurubis operates Europe's largest copper smelting and recycling network, but earnings are fundamentally constrained by global treatment and refining charges (TC/RCs), scrap spreads, and volatile energy costs. Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC hovers around 8-10%, failing the 12% hurdle.
column21: Historical ROCE/ROIC averages 8-10% across the cycle. Thin net margins (3-5%) fluctuate with global TC/RC benchmarks, byproduct acid prices, and energy costs. Inability to set prices independently of global commodity and smelting dynamics demonstrates lack of pricing power.

column14: Massive Verbund site integration yields internal energy and byproduct efficiency, but basic and intermediate chemicals face intense global commodity competition from low-cost US shale gas and severe Chinese overcapacity, leaving BASF without pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & commodity price-taker, REJECT). BASF's Verbund manufacturing integration cannot overcome structural commodity cyclicality, European energy cost disadvantages, and Chinese petrochemical overcapacity. Multi-cycle ROCE/ROIC averages 5-7%, well below the 12% hurdle.
column21: 5-year ROCE ranged from 1.7% to 13.7%, with 2023 at 4.5% and 2024 at 5.1% (median ~5.1%). Upstream petrochemicals and intermediates are price-takers facing structural margin compression from low-cost Middle Eastern/US feedstocks and domestic Chinese self-sufficiency.

column14: World-class Tier-1 copper (Collahuasi, Quellaveco) and iron ore assets provide resource longevity and low cash-cost curves, but Anglo American is a pure commodity price-taker with zero pricing power over global market clearing prices.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (commodity price-taker & volatile sub-hurdle ROIC, REJECT). Despite premier Tier-1 mineral deposits, Anglo American is a pure price-taker on global commodity exchanges. Realized earnings and returns swing wildly with macroeconomic cycles, lacking pricing power >= inflation.
column21: Attributable ROCE and ROIC swung violently from ~26% in 2021 to ~5-9% in 2023-2024, driven by commodity price slumps, high cost inflation, and multi-billion dollar asset write-downs (De Beers, Woodsmith). Revenues and operating margins are dictated entirely by global spot commodity benchmarks.

column14: Highly automated, low-carbon Nordic open-pit mining (Aitik, Garpenberg) and integrated smelting (Rönnskär, Odda) provide best-in-class European cost positioning, but Boliden is fundamentally a price-taker on LME copper/zinc prices and global smelter TC/RC benchmarks.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (commodity price-taker lacking pricing power, REJECT). Boliden is an admirably efficient, low-carbon Nordic mining and smelting operator, but its top-line realizations and cash flows are entirely dictated by LME spot metal prices (copper, zinc) and global smelting treatment charges. It possesses no pricing power.
column21: Operating margins and ROCE swing with global metal cycles (margins 9.7% in 2023 vs 18% in 2022). As an upstream producer of refined copper and zinc cathodes, sales occur at spot market benchmark prices with zero ability to independently raise prices against inflation.

column20: Fails Gate 1 (opaque proprietary commodity trading arm, REJECT). Glencore combines industrial mining with the world's largest commodity trading and marketing operation. The complex derivative books, counterparty credit commitments, and working capital arbitrage exposures of its Marketing division are opaque and fundamentally unverifiable from reported outside financial statements.
column21: Glencore's Marketing division generates hundreds of billions in gross volume using complex physical commodity trading, derivative hedging, and bilateral financing arrangements across opaque jurisdictions. Key risk exposures and mark-to-market valuations are not independently verifiable by external investors, triggering Gate 1 failure under standard (b).

column14: First-quartile low-cost Pilbara iron ore deposits and integrated automated heavy-haul rail and port terminals provide world-class cost leadership, but Rio Tinto is a pure commodity price-taker on global seaborne iron ore, copper, and aluminum benchmarks without pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (commodity price-taker lacking pricing power, REJECT). Despite world-class low-cost Pilbara iron ore assets and multi-cycle ROIC > 12%, Rio Tinto is an unhedged commodity price-taker. Realized earnings and cash flows fluctuate directly with global Platts iron ore and LME metal spot prices, offering zero pricing power >= inflation.
column21: Pilbara iron ore fines and lump sales are benchmarked to Platts 62% Fe index. Operating earnings swung from $30B+ in 2021 to ~$15B in 2023-2024 as iron ore prices normalized. Because iron ore is a bulk commodity, Rio Tinto cannot set prices above market clearing rates without forfeiting volumes.

column14: High-cost potash and salt miner lacking defensible cost leadership or pricing power. Global fertilizer price-taker subject to volatile commodity swings; multi-cycle ROCE averages ~3% (far below 12% hurdle), spiking only during temporary supply shocks (2022). Constrained by environmental brine disposal limits in German operations.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing). German potash and salt producer with structurally high production costs and significant environmental brine disposal constraints. Commodity price-taker whose margins follow volatile spot potash prices, resulting in multi-cycle median ROIC well below the 12% hurdle.
column21: Historical ROCE is structurally depressed: 1.9% in 2019, 0.0% in 2020, 3.2% in 2021, cyclically spiking to 25.7% in 2022 before fading to 11.2% in 2023 and ~3.2% in 2024. 5-year median ROIC is far below the 12% threshold. High fixed-cost underground mines in Germany face severe regulatory constraints over Werra river brine discharge.

column14: Global leader in nitrogen fertilizers and nitrates, but fundamentally a cyclical commodity price-taker. Lacks durable pricing power against global commodity cycles and suffers from structurally high European natural gas feedstock costs relative to North American and Middle Eastern peers. 5-year median ROIC (~7%) falls well short of the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing). World-scale nitrogen fertilizer producer exposed to global commodity price volatility and structurally disadvantaged European natural gas feedstock costs. Normalized ROIC averages 5-8%, well below the 12% threshold.
column21: Reported ROIC was 6.6% in 2019, 8.0% in 2020, 7.9% in 2021, cyclically spiking to 25.7% during the 2022 energy crisis, before plunging to 2.9% in 2023 and 5.0% in 2024. Multi-cycle median ROIC (~7%) is substantially below the 12% requirement. Feedstock exposure to volatile European natural gas undermines margin stability.

column14: Controls 1.3 million hectares of productive Swedish forest land and renewable hydro assets, constituting irreplaceable physical infrastructure. column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing). Exceptional owner of irreplaceable Swedish forestland and hydro power controlled by Lundberg, providing a generational store of real wealth. Biological forest asset yields are inherently low (2-3%), and paperboard/timber products lack independent pricing power against global forest product cycles.

Group ROCE averages 3-7% (failing 12% hurdle), burdened by heavy mill reinvestment capex.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing). Europe's largest private forest owner with world-class integrated mills, but commodity price-taking outputs (pulp, kraftliner, wood) and massive capital base result in multi-cycle Group ROCE of 3-6%, well below the 12% threshold.

Multi-cycle Group ROIC fails the 12% standard, and large-scale mill capex (Östrand, Obbola) absorbs substantial cash flow.

column21: Endeavour is an unhedged gold miner whose revenue is 100% determined by spot gold prices. Producing assets (Houndé, Ity, Sabodala-Massawa, Mana) are situated entirely in West Africa, where regional instability, military juntas (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger), and changing mining codes pose constant sovereign risk.

All physical operations are based in South Africa, where persistent power grid instability (Eskom load-shedding), deep-level mining cost inflation, and violent illicit mining ('zama-zamas') create severe operating hazards outside Western rule-of-law jurisdictions.

column21: Tangible ROIC consistently 19-22% (2022-2025) and recurring ROCE reached 11.2% in FY2025. Operating margin expanded >360 bps over 4 years to >20% under the ADVANCE program, outperforming upwardly revised targets. Multi-year Owner FCF conversion exceeds 115%. Balance sheet fortress with net debt / NI of 1.8x and interest coverage of ~60x (EBIT €4.97B vs interest €82.7M).

column14: Extensive manufacturing plant footprint and long-standing food service supply relationships provide customer proximity, but lack defensible barrier against rival converters. Unadjusted ROI of 9.5-10.9% falls short of the 12% ROIC hurdle. Fast-food chains and FMCG customers possess strong bargaining power, while single-use plastics regulations (EU SUP) drive recurring compliance and capex costs with limited pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% and lack of pricing power, REJECT). Finnish foodservice and flexible packaging converter is structurally constrained by powerful QSR and FMCG customer procurement, commodity resin/fiber price volatility, and tightening single-use plastics regulation, keeping multi-year returns on capital sub-hurdle (~9-10% ROI).
column21: Huhtamaki unadjusted ROI has hovered between 9.5% and 10.9% (2023-2025), failing the 12% ROIC hurdle. Operates as a contract packaging converter for concentrated buyers (e.g. McDonald's) with limited ability to pass through raw material cost spikes beyond standard contract lag. Facing structural regulatory headwinds from European single-use plastic restrictions.

column14: Cost-advantaged integrated pulp and paper mills provide low-cost position in virgin containerboard, but lack pricing power over cyclical swings. Industry capacity additions in Europe led to severe containerboard price cuts, causing ROCE to collapse from 23.7% in 2022 to 12.8% in 2023, 9.6% in 2024, and 6.7% in 2025.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% and lack of pricing power, REJECT). Integrated paper and packaging producer is a cyclical price-taker in containerboard and market pulp; chronic European industry capacity additions and weak demand depressed ROCE to 9.6% in 2024 and 6.7% in 2025.
column21: ROCE dropped from 23.7% in 2022 to 12.8% in 2023, 9.6% in 2024, and 6.7% in 2025 as the post-pandemic packaging boom normalized and massive industry capacity entered the market. Net debt increased to €2.6B (2.6x EBITDA) following the €609M Schumacher acquisition and heavy organic mill capex.

column14: Installed base of aseptic carton filling machines provides recurring sleeve demand, but #2 position behind dominant Tetra Pak and dilutive debt-funded M&A (Scholle IPN and Evergreen Asia) destroyed economic returns. Reported GAAP ROIC is 1.2% to 7.0% (5-year median 4.3%), well below the 12% hurdle, culminating in €351M non-recurring impairment charges and a net loss in 2025.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% and lack of pricing power, REJECT). Aseptic carton filling system installed base is overshadowed by Tetra Pak scale dominance and value-destructive M&A (Scholle IPN, Evergreen Asia) that loaded balance sheet with goodwill, resulting in 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 4.3% and a €351M impairment in 2025.
column21: 5-Year median GAAP ROIC is 4.3% (2.3% in 2022, 7.0% in 2023, 6.2% in 2024, and 1.2% in 2025), failing the 12% hurdle. Booked €350.7M in non-recurring impairments and charges in 2025, swinging to a net loss of -€87M. Long-term debt exceeds €2.0B with 2025 interest expense of €111M vs reported EBIT of €64M.

column14: Large Nordic forest landholdings and integrated pulp/board mills provide scale, but product lines are commoditized and exposed to graphic paper secular decline. Operational ROCE (excl. Forest) collapsed to 1.0% in 2023, 3.6% in 2024, and 2.7% in 2025, demonstrating complete absence of pricing power amidst global pulp and board cycles.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% and lack of pricing power, REJECT). Nordic forest products and packaging producer suffers from structural graphic paper decline, high wood input costs, and oversupply in consumer packaging board, dragging ROCE to 1.0-3.6% over 2023-2025.
column21: Operational ROCE excluding Forest was 20.9% at the 2022 commodity peak but plunged to 1.0% in 2023, 3.6% in 2024, and 2.7% in 2025 (5-year median ~3-4%, well below the 12% threshold). Heavy capex (Oulu conversion) and De Jong acquisition expanded debt (net debt reached €3.7B before forest sales) while returns stayed deeply sub-hurdle.

column14: Low-cost Paso de los Toros eucalyptus pulp mill in Uruguay and Nordic hydropower/forest assets offer scale advantages, but UPM remains an unhedged price-taker in global commodity pulp and declining graphic paper. ROCE dropped to 3.5% in 2023, 4.1% in 2024, and 5.5% in 2025, falling far below the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% and lack of pricing power, REJECT). Finnish forestry and pulp group is exposed to secular volume contraction in graphic paper and severe cyclicality in commodity market pulp, with multi-cycle ROCE of 3.5-5.5% over 2023-2025 failing the 12% hurdle.
column21: ROCE fell from 12.8% in 2022 to 3.5% in 2023, 4.1% in 2024, and 5.5% in 2025 (5-year median ~5.0%, far below 12%). Net debt rose to €3.0B following massive capital investment in the Uruguay pulp mill and Leuna biochemical refinery overruns, while graphic paper demand experiences persistent secular decline.

column11: Speculative commodity price-taker (silver/gold mining) with 100% of mining operations in Mexico subject to regulatory and security risks.
column20: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). World's largest primary silver producer, but an unhedged commodity price-taker with 100% of mining operations located in Mexico. Faces substantial Mexican mining-law reform risks, water permitting hurdles, and cartel security issues, with majority ownership (~75%) held by Industrias Peñoles.
column21: Fresnillo produces silver and gold across Mexican underground and open-pit mines. Operating profits fluctuate directly with COMEX/LBMA bullion spot prices, with no independent pricing power. Mining operations in Zacatecas and Sonora face operational disruption risks and escalating regulatory burdens in Mexico.

column11: Speculative commodity price-taker (precious metals mining) with operating assets concentrated in Peru, Argentina, and Brazil.
column20: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). Underground gold and silver miner operating in Peru, Argentina, and Brazil. A pure commodity price-taker exposed to bullion price volatility, recurring community protests/blockades in Peru, and Argentine currency/capital controls that impair cash repatriation.
column21: Core operations at Inmaculada and Pallancata (Peru) and San Jose (Argentina) face periodic operational suspensions, community negotiations, and political scrutiny over environmental permits. Free cash flow and returns on capital are deeply cyclical and governed entirely by global gold and silver prices.

column14: Adhesive formulation know-how (Bostik) and high-performance polymers (Pebax, Rilsan) face ongoing commoditization from Chinese producers in fluorochemicals and acrylics. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~7-8%, failing the 12% threshold (ROCE dropped to 7.8% in 2024).
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Despite strategic portfolio transformation toward specialty materials and adhesives (Bostik), Arkema remains exposed to cyclical commodity chemical headwinds, Chinese capacity additions in fluorochemicals/acrylics, and European industrial demand weakness. Multi-year after-tax GAAP ROIC of ~7-8% fails the 12% superinvestor hurdle.
column21: Recurring ROCE dropped from 15.5% at peak 2022 to 8.7% in 2023 and 7.8% in 2024, indicating after-tax GAAP ROIC well below 7%. Specialty operations lack the pricing power to offset severe upstream raw material inflation and Asian competition during cyclical downturns.

column14: Strong consumer paint brands (Dulux) and industrial coatings formulations, but compromised by lack of captive store distribution. Distribution through independent DIY big-box retailers exposes Akzo to channel bargaining power and raw material inflation (TiO2), resulting in a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 10.95% (< 12%).
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Akzo Nobel possesses recognizable decorative paint brands (Dulux, Sikkens), but lacks the captive direct-to-pro store network that underpins Sherwin-Williams' pricing power. Sells primarily through third-party DIY retailers and wholesale merchants, leaving margins exposed to raw material cycles (titanium dioxide) and resulting in a sub-hurdle 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 10.95%.
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 10.95% (2022: 7.6%, 2023: 10.3%, 2024: 11.6%, 2025: 12.3%) fails the 12% hurdle. Exposure to European retail channels and fierce competition from PPG and Axalta limits immediate pricing pass-through during input cost surges.

column14: Formulation co-development and regulatory lock-in with consumer care and pharmaceutical customers. Ingredients represent a tiny fraction of end-product cost but dictate efficacy and regulatory compliance, creating high switching costs; 5-year median ROIC is 14.2%.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Croda possesses proprietary formulation lock-in in beauty and pharma ingredients (median ROIC 14.2%), specialty chemicals has a Tier 3 industry persistence baseline (10-15Y). Prolonged customer destocking, normalization of post-COVID mRNA vaccine lipid demand, and rising competition from Asian bio-based synthesizers impose terminal headwinds on margin durability, capping CAP at 5 years.
column21: Post-tax ROIC fell sharply from 14.4% in 2022 to 8.3% in 2023 and 7.7% in 2024. Operating margins contracted from ~25% to 17.2% during destocking. Discontinuation of COVID lipid contract windfalls and integration of the lower-margin Iberchem acquisition highlight cyclical vulnerability in specialty chemicals.

column14: Proprietary flavour and fragrance formulation IP, captive aroma molecule palettes, and deep customer co-development create high switching barriers and pricing power in core fragrance and taste ingredients, though legacy animal nutrition assets severely depressed combined financial returns.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Firmenich brings world-class flavour and fragrance formulation IP, the combined entity remains constrained by the specialty chemicals cycle and legacy DSM vitamin exposure. The complex €18B merger, multi-billion write-downs, discounted ANH carve-out, and fragrance antitrust class-action settlements introduce severe structural uncertainty, capping CAP at 5 years (ROIC 2.4%).
column21: TTM GAAP ROIC is 2.4% (median 2.4%), with TTM net income of -€1,107m. Balance sheet carries over €15B in goodwill and intangibles post-merger. Animal Nutrition separation and global antitrust investigations illustrate deep restructuring headwinds that impair long-term compounding predictability.

column14: Proprietary high-performance polyamide compounding (EMS-Grivory) and automotive OEM co-development specifications create significant switching costs. Historical ROIC of 23-28% and ~27% EBIT margins provide empirical proof of moat, though auto OEM customer concentration poses erosion threats.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While EMS-Chemie possesses high ROIC and disciplined family ownership, ~60%+ direct exposure to global automotive manufacturing faces severe terminal headwinds from European auto de-industrialization, shift to Chinese EV ecosystems, and commoditization pressure from rival polyamide producers.
column21: Multi-year ROIC averages ~25-28% with operating margins around 26-28% and pristine net-cash balance sheet. However, over 60% of revenue stems from automotive applications (Grivory metal replacement and EFTEC adhesives). European automotive volume stagnation and aggressive Asian competition limit predictable competitive advantage period to well below the 15-year threshold.

column14: Specialty additives and process know-how face commoditization and volatile cyclical demand. 5-year average ROIC of ~5.0% and operating margins of 3-7% fail to demonstrate structural moat or economic pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Evonik's 5-year average ROIC of ~5.0% and operating margins of 3-7% demonstrate a severe lack of pricing power and structural moat. The portfolio suffers from commodity cyclicality in animal nutrition (methionine) and high European energy costs.
column21: Evonik reports a 5-year average ROIC of ~5.0% and operating margins fluctuating between -2.3% and 7.3%, failing the 12% GAAP ROIC threshold. Inability to consistently pass through raw material and energy cost inflation highlights commodity price-taker dynamics in major product lines.

column14: Formulation know-how across >10,000 tailored specialty lubricants where fluid cost is <1-2% of machine operating cost, making customer switching irrational due to catastrophic failure risk. Proven pricing power with >20% price increases passed through in 2022-2023, sustaining GAAP ROIC >17% and tangible ROIC >22%.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global independent leader in specialty lubricants and functional fluids. Asymmetric value proposition where fluid cost is negligible compared to catastrophic downtime risk of unlubricated machinery. Fortress net-cash balance sheet and multi-decade family owner-operator discipline. [5-10Y g: specialty/industrial volume net of ICE fade 1.5% + price/mix 2.0% + operating leverage 0.5% + bolt-on M&A and dividends 1.5%]
column21: 17.7% GAAP ROIC and 22.5% operating ROIC with ~97% FCF conversion. Pristine debt-free balance sheet with €223M cash and interest coverage >34x. Demonstrated pricing power through >20% cumulative price realization during 2022-2023 raw material inflation.

column14: Global leader in flavors and fragrances where proprietary formulations represent <2% of customer COGS but dictate 100% of sensory identity. Massive switching barriers protect customer relationships. Demonstrated pricing power recovering 100% of input cost spikes, sustaining 14-16% GAAP ROIC and >36% tangible ROIC.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global #1 sensory toll booth owning proprietary flavor and fragrance formulas at <2% of customer COGS. Indispensable taste and scent partner for global CPG giants with proven pricing power and >36% tangible ROIC. [5-10Y g: organic volume/mix 3.0% + local price net of structural CHF FX drag 0.5% + margin expansion/deleveraging 1.0% + bolt-on M&A 0.5%]
column21: GAAP ROIC of ~14.2% and operating/tangible ROIC of ~36.8% with 105.8% FCF conversion. Pristine interest coverage of 12.5x and net debt repayable in 2.9 years. Successfully passed through 100% of raw material inflation through 6-9% pricing adjustments with zero client loss.

column14: PGM catalyst chemistry and refining know-how face cyclical automotive exposure and lack pricing power against major OEMs. Multi-year ROCE and ROIC languish at 6-8%, falling far short of the 12% threshold.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Multi-year ROCE and GAAP ROIC of 6-8% fall well short of the 12% hurdle. The core Clean Air autocatalyst business faces structural terminal headwinds from vehicle electrification, compounded by past value-destructive capital allocation missteps in battery materials.
column21: 5-year average ROCE and GAAP ROIC languish at 6-8%, failing the 12% threshold. Core operating profit remains heavily reliant on ICE emission catalysts undergoing secular decline, while historical abortive attempts to pivot into battery materials resulted in £300M+ in asset write-downs.

column14: Global undisputed leader in industrial enzymes and microbial cultures, with unmatched strain libraries and fermentation scale. Enzymes cost 1-3% of customer COGS but deliver critical performance, locking in CPG clients. Proven pricing power (4-7% annual pricing) with multi-cycle operating ROIC >25%.
column20: Passes all 6 gates. Global powerhouse in industrial enzymes and biosolutions following the Novozymes/Chr. Hansen merger, anchored by Novo Holdings stewardship. Irreplaceable biological catalysts at 1-3% of customer COGS, benefiting secularly from decarbonization and green chemistry. [5-10Y g: organic biosolutions volume 4.5% + price/mix 1.5% + merger revenue synergies & operating leverage 1.0% + bolt-on M&A 0.5%]
column21: Operating ROIC of ~29% with 113.9% FCF conversion (€730M FCF in FY2025). Robust balance sheet with 11.9x interest coverage and long-term ownership backing by Novo Holdings. Successfully pushed 4-7% annual pricing through inflationary cycles while maintaining ~36% EBITDA margins.

column14: Architectural and structural engineering specification moat in concrete admixtures, Sikaflex sealants, and roofing membranes where chemical cost is <1-2% of project capex but product failure causes catastrophic damage (30x cost). Demonstrated pricing power by expanding material margin from 53.6% (2023) to 54.9% (2025) through retained input cost deflation.
column20: Specification-driven moat in concrete admixtures and construction sealants where chemical cost is <2% of build cost but failure risk is 30x. Material margins expanded to ~55% via retained input deflation; rapid post-MBCC deleveraging with >100% FCF conversion. [5-10Y g: organic infra/repair volume 3.5% + pricing power net of CHF FX drag 0.5% + MBCC synergies and deleveraging 1.5% + selective bolt-on M&A 1.5%]
column21: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 14.0% with operating/tangible ROIC exceeding 50%. Material margin expanded from 53.6% in 2023 to 54.9% in 2025. MBCC integration captured CHF 182M+ in cumulative synergies, elevating MBCC EBITDA margins from 15% to >20%. FY2025 operating FCF reached CHF 1.35B (12.1% of sales), reducing net debt to CHF 3.0B with interest coverage of ~9.6x.

column14: High customer switching costs via co-developed flavor and fragrance formulations and proprietary pet food palatants (Diana Division). Ingredient costs represent <2% of finished consumer goods price, supporting tangible ROIC >15% and gross margin stability.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Long-term runway is impaired by global antitrust investigations into flavor/fragrance cartel pricing, decelerating volume growth, and aggressive M&A rollups (Swedencare, ADF/IDF) that diluted multi-year GAAP ROIC to 7-9%.
column21: Multi-year GAAP ROIC averaged 7.0-9.0% between 2021 and 2025, heavily diluted by €2.7B in goodwill and intangibles. The company faced cross-border antitrust probes into alleged fragrance price-fixing and forced regulatory remedies on pet food assets. Decelerating organic volume growth and FMCG customer consolidation curtail economic moat visibility below the 15-year hurdle.

column14: Specialty polymer formulation know-how and aerospace composite qualifications provide customer stickiness, but the business fails the empirical proof-of-moat test: ROCE is sub-hurdle at 8.1-8.8%, organic EBITDA fell 12% in FY2025, and fluoropolymers face persistent, multi-billion-dollar PFAS regulatory bans and environmental litigation liabilities.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing, REJECT). Capital efficiency fails hurdle with ROCE of 8.1-8.8% and EBITDA contracting 12% in FY2025. Fluoropolymer portfolio carries material terminal PFAS regulatory liabilities and environmental remediation costs.
column21: Spun off from Solvay in Dec 2023, Syensqo generated ROCE of only 8.1-8.8% in 2024-2025, well below the 12% ROIC requirement. FY2025 net sales fell 3% to €6.14B and underlying EBITDA dropped 12% organically to €1.21B due to volume declines across Specialty Polymers and Technology Solutions. Ongoing PFAS environmental liabilities include a €167M NJDEP settlement and severe EU regulatory phase-out risks.

column14: Proprietary metallurgy and catalytic formulation know-how are completely overwhelmed by massive capital destruction in EV battery cathode materials, resulting in a €1.60B impairment and a net loss of -€1.48B in FY2024. The legacy ICE automotive catalyst cash cow faces secular terminal obsolescence, while cathode materials generate recurring operating losses (-€91M EBIT in 2025).
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing, REJECT). Massive capital allocation failure in EV battery cathode materials triggered a €1.60B impairment and €1.48B net loss in FY2024. Core automotive catalyst earnings face terminal secular headwinds from ICE phase-out.
column21: Umicore recorded a €1.60B impairment on its Battery Materials assets in 2024, driving reported FY2024 net profit to -€1.48B and crushing multi-year GAAP ROIC. In FY2025, Battery Materials Solutions continued to post an adjusted EBIT loss of -€91M. The automotive catalyst business (Catalysis segment) faces secular terminal decline as global light-duty vehicles transition away from internal combustion engines.

column14: North American Stainless (NAS) possesses a favorable regional cost position, but the business operates as a cyclical commodity price-taker lacking pricing power above inflation across the cycle. Margins are dictated by global stainless base prices, scrap/nickel surcharges, and Chinese overcapacity; FY2025 swung to a net loss of -€40M with ROCE averaging well below the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing, REJECT). Commodity stainless steel price-taker subject to severe cyclical margin swings and global/Chinese overcapacity. 5-year average ROCE is ~9% and FY2025 swung to a net loss of -€40M; profit engine NAS relies heavily on US tariff protection rather than a structural customer moat.
column21: Reported ROCE fell to 9.0% in FY2024, and FY2025 recorded a net loss of -€40M on €5.78B revenue due to depressed stainless base prices, European weakness, and inventory write-downs. Net debt expanded to €1.2B following the €820M acquisition of Haynes International. Stainless steel base prices and alloy surcharges fluctuate directly with underlying commodity quotes, demonstrating zero independent pricing power.

column14: Massive scale and vertically integrated iron ore mining provide an operational cost buffer, but ArcelorMittal remains an undifferentiated commodity price-taker whose margins fluctuate with global steel spreads, iron ore costs, and Chinese export dumping. 5-year normalized ROIC is sub-hurdle at ~2.5-3.5%, far below the 12% cost-of-capital threshold.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing, REJECT). Capital-intensive commodity steelmaker with normalized ROIC of ~2.5-3.5%, failing the 12% hurdle. Entirely a price-taker on global steel spreads, facing intense Chinese export competition and heavy decarbonization capex requirements in Europe.
column21: Normalized ROIC averaged ~2.5-3.5% across 2024-2025. EBITDA per tonne contracted to $121/t in FY2025 as European steel spreads remained compressed by Chinese imports and elevated energy costs. Net debt rose to $7.9B in FY2025. The business requires billions in ongoing maintenance and decarbonization capex (DRI/EAF transition) while lacking pricing power over finished steel products.

column14: Hardox and Strenx high-strength steels possess recognized brand equity and proprietary quenching/tempering know-how in heavy machinery wear plates. However, commoditized standard steel (SSAB Europe and SSAB Americas) constitutes the majority of production volume, where SSAB is an absolute price taker vulnerable to global steel price swings and cheap foreign imports. Returns are severely cyclical, with 10-year median ROIC ~7-10%, failing the 12% threshold. Massive green steel transition capex at the Luleå and Oxelösund mini-mills threatens further capital efficiency drag.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Niche leadership in Hardox/Strenx high-strength steel cannot offset commodity price-taker dynamics in standard European and American steel sheets/plates. 10-year cycle-average ROIC hovers around 7-10%, well below the 12% hurdle. Decarbonization transition (fossil-free steel capex in Luleå) locks up massive capital in a cyclical, low-return industry.
column21: SSAB's 10-year historical ROIC averages 7-10%, swinging from 20%+ during post-COVID steel price spikes to near-zero/negative during industrial downturns. Consolidated margins are dictated by global iron ore, coking coal, and hot-rolled coil prices rather than proprietary pricing power. The multi-billion SEK transformation of Luleå into a fossil-free mini-mill requires sustained high capex, depressing incremental returns on invested capital.

column14: No durable economic moat exists across the conglomerate. Thyssenkrupp Steel Europe suffers from structural cost disadvantages (high German electricity, carbon, and unionized labor costs) and chronic global overcapacity. Automotive Technology operates in low-margin contract manufacturing facing relentless OEM price-down pressure. Decades of conglomerate restructuring, multi-billion-euro asset impairments, and massive legacy pension burdens (~€2.5B+) confirm the total absence of economic moat.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Moat Archetype None & ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Chronic value-destroying conglomerate with negative-to-low single-digit 10-year ROIC. Trapped by high German industrial energy costs, legacy pension liabilities, OEM automotive pricing pressure, and multi-billion decarbonization capex requirements for Duisburg steelworks.
column21: 10-year ROIC has persistently lagged WACC, frequently turning negative due to repeated hundred-million-euro asset impairments and restructuring charges. Steel Europe has generated chronic operating losses, requiring ongoing carve-out attempts and government subsidies. Net debt and multi-billion-euro pension liabilities constrain capital allocation, eliminating any capacity for compounding per-share intrinsic value.

column14: Global market leadership in railway switch systems and proprietary specialty processing in High Performance Metals provide technological niche barriers. However, heavy consolidated exposure to cyclical European automotive and industrial end-markets dilutes returns. 10-year ROCE/ROIC averages 5-7%, falling well short of the 12% cost-of-capital hurdle. Decarbonization capex ('greentec steel' electric arc furnaces in Linz and Donawitz) further burdens multi-year free cash flow.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Niche engineering strength in railway turnouts and tool steel cannot insulate the group from European automotive and steel industrial cyclicality. 10-year average ROCE/ROIC of 5-7% fails the 12% compounding hurdle, while green steel electric arc transition capex absorbs substantial operational cash flow.
column21: 10-year historical ROCE/ROIC has averaged between 5% and 7%, dipping to 3-5% during industrial downturns and only temporarily exceeding 12% during peak post-pandemic supply constraints. The business is heavily exposed to the European automotive sector (>30% of sales), facing structural volume stagnation and cost inflation in domestic Austrian energy.

column14: Owns prime central London office campuses (Broadgate, Regent's Place) and retail parks with significant planning barriers to entry. However, commercial real estate yields are structurally low (4-6%), producing a 10-year average ROIC of only 2.5-5.0%, far below the 12% hurdle. Commercial lease rents are negotiated tenant expenses, highly vulnerable to hybrid work office downsizing, corporate tenant restructurings, and cyclical interest rate shocks.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Prime London office campuses and retail parks face structural cap-rate realities, generating multi-year ROIC of only 2.5-5.0% against a 12% hurdle. Commercial rents lack true inflation pricing power, as tenants downsize office footprints amid hybrid working and higher borrowing costs depress property asset values.
column21: 10-year historical GAAP ROIC averages 2.5-5.0%, heavily depressed by periodic commercial property revaluation write-downs during UK interest rate increases. Total Accounting Return (TAR) targets of 8-10% rely on asset leverage rather than superior unlevered operational returns. Office portfolio faces persistent structural occupancy and lease renewal headwinds from corporate remote/hybrid working models.

column14: High-density urban assets in Paris, Milan, and major German cities have prime location value and planning constraints. However, consolidated capital efficiency is structurally constrained by commercial real estate cap rates, generating a 10-year ROIC of just 3.0-4.0% vs the 12% hurdle. Pricing power is actively suppressed by German residential rent regulations, post-COVID office space consolidation, and cyclical hospitality demand.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Diversified European REIT with 10-year historical ROIC of 3-4%, structurally incapable of meeting the 12% capital compounding hurdle. Lacks genuine pricing power: German residential units face statutory rent caps, while European offices face hybrid working occupancy pressures and higher debt refinancing rates.
column21: 10-year historical ROIC hovers between 3.1% and 3.7%, constrained by asset-heavy real estate balance sheets and conservative net rental yields. German residential portfolio (~30% of assets) is subject to stringent German tenant protections and rent caps, capping rental escalation. European office portfolio faces tenant footprint compression, leading to portfolio revaluation write-downs in rising rate environments.

column14: Prime central London commercial developments and dominant regional shopping destinations possess unreplicable physical locations and complex planning approvals. However, commercial real estate asset intensity results in a 10-year average ROIC of only 3.0-4.0%, failing the 12% compounding hurdle. Landsec cannot enforce pricing power above inflation without driving tenant vacancies, lease renegotiations, or retail tenant failures during consumer downturns.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Flagship UK commercial property portfolio generates 10-year historical ROIC of only 3.0-4.0%, structurally trailing the 12% hurdle. Real estate rental yields cannot achieve compounding quality standards without excessive debt leverage, while London office demand and shopping center leasing face persistent tenant rationalization.
column21: 10-year historical GAAP ROIC averages in the 3.0-3.9% range, heavily affected by multi-billion-pound property revaluation deficits during UK rate-hiking cycles. Retail tenant restructuring (CVAs) and persistent hybrid working adoption across London office occupiers constrain lease renewal pricing power and cap total accounting returns.

column14: Iberian commercial office, logistics, and shopping centre portfolio with prime Madrid/Barcelona locations; sub-3% ROIC fails the 12% hurdle, and high-capex pivot to data centres requires heavy equity dilution and execution risk.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 2.7%, REJECT). Spain's largest REIT fails capital efficiency hurdles with unlevered portfolio yields of 4.5-5.5% and historical ROIC under 3%. High-capex data centre pivot brings substantial equity dilution and execution risk.
column21: Merlin Properties is Spain's largest SOCIMI with ~€11.5B GAV across Madrid/Barcelona offices (50%+), logistics (25%+), and shopping centres. 5-year average ROIC sits between 2.5% and 3.0%, well below the 12% hurdle. Net debt stands at €3.35B (~28% LTV, ~8.8x net debt/EBITDA). A €1B equity capital increase was executed in mid-2024 to fund data centre development across Madrid, Barcelona, and the Basque Country, illustrating high capital intensity and external financing dependence.

column14: Pan-European elderly care-home portfolio with long triple-net leases; unlevered returns on capital of 3-5% fail the 12% ROIC threshold, and care-home operator solvency fragility limits real rental pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 4.2%, REJECT). Pan-European healthcare REIT fails capital efficiency hurdles with unlevered portfolio yields of 5.3-5.5% and ROIC < 5%. Fragile care-home operator economics and state reimbursement caps prevent real pricing power.
column21: Aedifica manages a €6.0B+ healthcare portfolio of ~600 properties across Belgium, Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, and Nordics.
