column21: Reported 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 7.72%, capped by ARERA regulatory allowances. FY2024 capex of €2.59B exceeds operating cash flow of €1.48B, producing structural cash flow deficits. Net debt of €9.10B (8.57x net income) and gross debt of €11.41B (10.75x net income) breach the Gate 6 threshold of <=4.0x. Continuous reliance on debt issuance to sustain capital programs and dividend payouts violates balance sheet independence from the kindness of strangers.

column14: Long-dated hydroelectric concessions along the Danube and Austrian Alps with run-of-river and pumped-storage plants operating at the bottom of the European merit order. Strong historical 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 21.0% driven by zero-fuel-cost hydro generation, though earnings are exposed to wholesale merchant power price volatility and statutory windfall profit taxes.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (gate_6 = N, REJECT). Austria's dominant hydroelectric generator possessing irreplaceable dam concessions, but fails Gate 6 Pillar 1 peak-to-peak earnings power compounding. Record FY2023 earnings (€6.52 Owner EPS) represented an unrepeatable energy crisis windfall spike; earnings have collapsed significantly as European wholesale power prices normalized (€4.29 Owner EPS in FY2025). Furthermore, Austria has extended statutory windfall taxes on inframarginal hydro through 2030, capping upside while downside volume risk (droughts) remains unhedged.
column21: While Verbund maintains a low-leverage balance sheet (Net Debt/NI of 1.04x) and strong multi-year GAAP ROIC (21.0% median), its earnings fail Gate 6 Pillar 1. FY2023 net income of €2.27B and EPS of €6.52 were driven by historical European energy crisis gas and power price spikes. As wholesale power prices normalized, net income contracted by 34% to €1.49B (€4.29 EPS) in FY2025. Austrian statutory extension of the Energy Crisis Contribution (windfall tax) through 2030 permanently skims supernormal profits, leaving the company exposed to commodity power swings and weather volatility without secular peak-to-peak compounding.

column14: Statutory network monopoly over ~11,000 km of high-pressure gas transport pipelines and 4 LNG regasification terminals in Spain. Insurmountable physical and concession barriers to entry, with inflation-indexed regulated asset base returns set by CNMC.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Spanish gas TSO and LNG terminal operator faces Tier 4 regulated utility baseline (5-10Y) and severe Macrotrend 4 (Energy Transition) terminal headwinds from EU natural gas phase-out, declining domestic gas demand, and unproven hydrogen backbone returns.
column21: Spanish CNMC caps allowed financial return on RAB at 5.44% (2021-2026) and 6.46% (2027-2032), capping historical 4-year median GAAP ROIC at 8.15%. FY24 net loss of -€299.3M due to Tallgrass Energy impairment, recovering to €339.1M in FY25. With long-term gas volume decline under EU decarbonization targets, competitive advantage period is capped at 10 years.

column14: Statutory municipal gas distribution concession monopoly across Italy (>50% market share following 2i Rete Gas acquisition). Returns protected by ARERA inflation-indexed RAB framework.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). Regulated Italian gas distributor carries extreme leverage (€10.4B debt vs €672M net income, >15x debt/NI) and sub-hurdle 7.2% ROIC due to ARERA-capped returns and continuous debt-funded capex dilution for 2i Rete Gas and network digitisation.
column21: ARERA regulates tariffs yielding a 4-year median GAAP ROIC of 7.17% (FY22: 5.9%, FY23: 6.8%, FY24: 7.5%, FY25: 8.0%). Following the €5.3B acquisition of 2i Rete Gas, net debt reached ~€9.9B to €11B against FY25 net income of €672.3M (14.7x net debt/NI), with interest coverage of 5.19x. Capex of €1.09B exceeds D&A of €712M, requiring perpetual debt refinancing and equity rights issues.

column14: Niche LPG and downstream fuel distribution terminals in French overseas territories, Caribbean, and Africa, but lacks pricing power against regulated local fuel caps and commodity price volatility.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (REJECT). French downstream energy and LPG distributor lacks pricing power and generates sub-12% consolidated ROIC (9-11%) due to local fuel price caps in emerging/island markets, wholesale fuel price exposure, and heavy capital commitments into Photosol solar projects.
column21: Consolidated ROCE/ROIC tracks between 9.0% and 11.5%, failing the 12% GAAP / 15% tangible ROIC threshold. Energy distribution is exposed to retail fuel price controls in developing markets and volatile volume margins. The divestment of Rubis Terminal (2024) reduced infrastructure toll assets while capex shifted into capital-intensive solar PV generation (Photosol).

column14: Statutory network monopoly over ~38,000 km of Italian gas transmission pipelines, 17 Bcm of storage capacity, and LNG terminals, with ARERA inflation-indexed RAB returns.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). Italian gas transmission monopoly carries €14.4B debt (net debt ~€19B in 2025/2026) vs €1.24B net income (11.6x debt/NI), thin 4.6x interest coverage, and capped 7.6% ROIC with annual capex (€2.7B) exceeding D&A (€1.0B) by nearly 3x.
column21: 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 7.57% (FY22: 4.57%, FY23: 7.74%, FY24: 7.95%, FY25: 7.39%), capped by ARERA regulatory parameters. Long-term debt of €14.37B and net debt of ~€19.0B severely exceed the 4.0x net debt/NI baseline (11.6x-15.4x). FY25 interest coverage is 4.58x (below the 5.0x minimum threshold), with ongoing capex of €2.7B requiring continuous debt issuance.

column14: Owns Cruachan pumped-storage hydro and large-scale biomass generation units, but lacks pricing power due to wholesale electricity price-taker status and heavy dependence on government biomass subsidies (ROC cliff in 2027).
column20: Fails Gate 3b (REJECT). UK power generator operates as a wholesale commodity price taker whose margins depend on power/gas/pellet spreads and government subsidy schemes. Lucrative legacy ROC biomass subsidies expire in 2027, transitioning to a lower-margin dispatchable CfD bridge.
column21: Core biomass generation at Drax Power Station is exposed to global wood pellet supply costs, shipping freight, and UK wholesale power prices. Expiration of ROC subsidies in March 2027 marks a sharp reduction in subsidy yields. Operating margins and ROIC fluctuate with merchant spark spreads and government policy rather than autonomous pricing power.

column14: Low-cost Nordic hydro and nuclear generation assets are physically irreplaceable, but Fortum is a pure wholesale commodity price taker on Nord Pool with zero pricing power.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (REJECT). Nordic clean power generator operates as a wholesale price taker on Nord Pool. Returns on capital and cash flows fluctuate violently with volatile Nordic spot power prices, hydrological reservoir levels, and carbon allowance prices.
column21: Over 80% of comparable EBITDA stems from wholesale power generation (hydro and nuclear in Finland and Sweden). Because electricity is a commoditized product dispatched via merit order, Fortum has no ability to raise prices independently. Capital efficiency and ROIC swing cyclically with wholesale power prices and weather patterns.

column14: Wholesale merchant power generator transitioning from coal/lignite to offshore/onshore wind and solar. Operates as a commodity price-taker on wholesale European electricity markets with zero structural pricing power above spot clearing rates. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~5-6% (2021: 4.4%, 2022: -3.6%, 2023: 8.6%, 2024: 5.9%), failing the 12% hurdle.
column20: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & merchant commodity pricing, REJECT). RWE operates primarily as an independent power producer and energy trader exposed to wholesale electricity spot market swings. Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC is structurally below 6%, falling far short of the 12% hurdle, while heavy renewable capex continuously dilutes returns on capital.
column21: Multi-year ROIC averages ~5% over 2021-2024 (4.4% in 2021, -3.6% in 2022, 8.6% in 2023, 5.9% in 2024). Electricity is a non-differentiated commodity price-taker product. Capital expenditure program for green transition requires heavy debt funding without pricing power protection.

column14: Entrenched local distribution concessions (electricity and gas), district heating grids, and waste-to-energy assets in Milan, Brescia, and Lombardy create local infrastructure monopolies. Operating tangible ROIC exceeds 16-20% due to local concession scale, though regulatory returns are capped by ARERA.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Balance sheet leverage & capex dilution, REJECT). Lombardy multi-utility with protected local concession networks, but net debt of €4.15B is 5.5x net income (€750M), exceeding the 4.0x ceiling. Heavy continuous capex (€1.68B vs €955M D&A) depresses multi-year free cash flow conversion to ~69%, requiring persistent debt reliance.
column21: FY2022-2025 net income averaged ~€670M while capex expanded from €1.24B to €1.68B annually, generating negative pure free cash flow in FY2023 and FY2024. Long-term debt stands at €6.03B against €1.88B cash, yielding net debt / net income of 5.5x. Regulated tariff cap keeps median GAAP ROIC at ~10%.

column20: Fails Gate 1 (Understandability / Opaque trading book, REJECT). Centrica's earnings are heavily driven by Centrica Energy (formerly Energy Marketing & Trading), a large proprietary energy trading and optimization book that swings wildly and cannot be verified from the outside. Combined with retail supply subject to Ofgem price caps and nuclear/storage assets, the economic engine lacks transparent, predictable compounding.
column21: Centrica Energy operating profits fluctuated from £1.4B in 2022 to £774M in 2023 and £307M in 2024 due to market volatility. British Gas retail margins remain constrained by the UK default tariff price cap, and upstream asset dependencies make earnings unpredictable.

column14: Regulated French natural gas infrastructure (GRDF distribution and GRTgaz transmission) combined with hydro concessions form an irreplaceable toll-booth infrastructure network. Regulated asset base provides inflation indexing, supporting operating tangible ROIC of ~18-22%.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Balance sheet leverage & interest coverage, REJECT). Core French utility with extensive regulated networks, but net debt of €25.5B is 6.9x net income (€3.69B) and total debt is €40.0B (10.9x NI). EBIT interest coverage of 3.45x falls well below the 5.0x fortress threshold, with volatile cash conversion due to working capital and heavy transition capex.
column21: FY2025 net debt stood at €25.5B (€40.0B long-term debt against €14.5B cash) against net income of €3.69B. Interest expense of €2.58B against EBIT of €8.89B leaves interest coverage at 3.45x, failing Gate 6 balance sheet criteria. FY2025 OCF was negative (-€1.48B) due to working capital swings alongside €7.27B capex.

column14: Europe's largest distribution system operator with 1.6 million kilometers of energy networks across Germany and CEE. Regulated asset base (RAB) creates a physically unreplicable natural monopoly with guaranteed regulatory returns under BNetzA oversight.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Massive debt burden & weak interest coverage, REJECT). Dominant European distribution grid operator, but carries economic net debt of €43.2B (net financial debt €32.5B) against net income of €1.73B (18.7x net financial debt / NI). Interest coverage of 2.36x severely breaches the 5.0x threshold, driven by massive continuous grid capex requiring constant debt refinancing.
column21: FY2025 interest expense of €2.20B on EBIT of €5.21B gives interest coverage of only 2.36x. Economic net debt of €43.24B (including pension obligations and AROs) and financial debt of €37.3B tower over net income of €1.73B. Annual capex of €7.94B exceeded operating cash flow of €7.00B.

column14: Protected municipal concession monopolies in integrated water management, waste collection/treatment, and gas distribution in Emilia-Romagna and northern Italy. Operating tangible ROIC exceeds 25%, protected by regional municipal shareholding and ARERA regulatory tariffs.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Balance sheet leverage & interest coverage, REJECT). High-quality Italian multi-utility with excellent municipal management, but net debt of €3.44B represents 7.4x net income (€464M), well above the 4.0x limit. Interest coverage of 4.94x fails the 5.0x fortress requirement, with heavy ongoing capex (€1.03B vs €590M D&A) absorbing operational cash flow.
column21: Net debt of €3.44B (€4.29B debt less €845M cash) against FY2025 net income of €464.3M results in 7.4x leverage. EBIT of €891.3M vs interest expense of €180.5M yields 4.94x interest coverage, below the 5.0x threshold. Regulated returns structurally capped at 6-8%.

column14: Regulated natural gas and electricity distribution concessions hold local natural monopoly positions in Spain and Latin America, but allowed returns are politically capped by the CNMC (financial remuneration rate ~5.58% for electricity distribution and ~5.44% for gas distribution). The merchant generation and energy supply divisions are price-takers in volatile wholesale electricity and LNG markets, exposed to state clawbacks (topes al gas) and windfall taxes. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~8% (ranging from 6.5% to 11.1%), failing the 12% hurdle, with no autonomous pricing power >= inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Spanish multi-utility with regulated gas and power networks and merchant generation. Regulated asset base remuneration is capped at ~5.5-6.5% by the CNMC, while merchant power and gas commercialization face wholesale price volatility, regulatory clawback interventions, and windfall taxes. Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC is sub-hurdle (~8%), lacking genuine pricing power >= inflation.
column21: Consolidated EBITDA hovered around €5.3B-€5.5B across 2023-2025 with net debt at €12.3B (~2.3x EBITDA). Historical reported ROIC stood at 6.5% in 2018 and averaged ~8-9% over the 2018-2024 strategic plan, only briefly reaching 11.1% in 2024 and 11.3% in 2025 during elevated European gas/power sparks, well short of the 12% cycle-neutral hurdle. Shifting shareholder dynamics (CriteriaCaixa, CVC, GIP, IFM) and aborted split plans (Project Gemini) reflect ongoing strategic and regulatory frictions.

column14: Global leader in water, waste, and energy services with over 70% of revenue protected by long-term municipal concessions (10-30 years) and industrial contracts containing contractual inflation indexation formulas (CPI/labor/energy). High switching barriers in specialized hazardous waste treatment and municipal water treatment plants. Successfully integrated Suez, expanding GAAP ROIC from 7.37% in 2022 to 12.07% in 2025 as cumulative post-merger synergies exceeded €500M.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Peace-of-Mind Balance Sheet & Leverage, REJECT). Global ecological services champion with defensible water and waste concessions and contractual inflation indexation. However, capital-intensive utility structure carries €16.5B in long-term debt and €9.1B in net debt against €1.2B in TTM net income (Net Debt / NI = 7.5x, well above the 4.0x ceiling), with interest coverage of only 3.65x failing the > 5.0x cycle threshold (consistent with sub-industry g6_default=N).
column21: FY2025 revenue reached €44.4B with EBITDA of €6.8B and EBIT of €3.2B. Post-Suez integration drove GAAP ROIC up to 12.07% in FY25 (4-year median 10.25%, ROCE after-tax 9.4%). While Owner FCF conversion is robust (>100% of NI), balance sheet leverage remains structurally elevated post-Suez with long-term debt of €16,541M and net debt of €9,101M against net income of €1,217M (debt repayment time > 7 years). FY25 interest expense of €876M yields EBIT interest coverage of 3.65x, violating the Gate 6 fortress baseline (> 5.0x).

column14: Infrastructure construction contracting operates under competitive fixed-price bidding with thin operating margins (3-6%) and persistent exposure to cost overruns. The energy division (Acciona Energía) generates power from wind and solar farms, selling an undifferentiated commodity into wholesale merchant power markets that suffer from renewable price cannibalization (capture price erosion during high wind/solar output). Consolidated group ROIC is chronically depressed at ~2-4%, failing the 12% hurdle, with no pricing power >= inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Conglomerate spanning civil engineering construction contracting and merchant renewable energy generation (Acciona Energía). Construction faces cyclical competitive bidding and cost overruns, while renewable power sells commodity electrons exposed to power price drops and negative capture pricing. Consolidated ROIC is structurally sub-hurdle (~2-4%), failing to cover its cost of capital.
column21: Consolidated EBITDA grew to €2.5B in 2024 and €3.2B in 2025 aided by asset rotations at Acciona Energía and turnaround at Nordex, with Net Debt of €7.0B (~2.2x-2.9x EBITDA). However, multi-cycle group ROIC remains severely depressed at 1.8%-3.5%, consistently below WACC (~6.5%). The merchant power segment lacks pricing power against wholesale power price declines and Spanish regulatory windfall interventions, while the infrastructure division operates in high-risk lump-sum EPC contracts.

column14: Global pure-play onshore wind and solar developer. While holding extensive grid connection permits and project pipelines, the business model produces undifferentiated commodity electricity with zero independent pricing power. Long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) and government Contracts for Difference (CfDs) lock in fixed nominal strike prices that fail to adjust for severe capital expenditure inflation (turbines, transformers, balance of plant), while the asset-rotation funding model (selling stakes in operational farms to institutional buyers) stalled as global interest rates rose. 5-year median ROIC is severely sub-hurdle at 2.5-4%.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Pure-play global wind and solar developer producing commodity power. PPA strike prices provide no pricing power against capex and supply-chain cost surges, while merchant power volumes face severe price cannibalization. Asset rotation model disrupted by higher global discount rates. Historical ROIC of 2.5-4% fails the 12% hurdle.
column21: Net debt expanded to €8.3B in 2024 and stabilized at ~€8.1B in 2025 following heavy growth capex and European minority portfolio buyouts. Post-tax ROIC hovered between 2.5% and 4.0% across 2023-2025, consistently lagging the company's cost of capital. PPA execution in the US and Europe faced declining realized off-take prices, while rising cost of debt severely compressed equity internal rates of return (IRRs), forcing management to pull back growth targets to defend balance sheet metrics.

column14: Global pioneer in offshore wind development. The economic engine was devastated by severe cost inflation, installation vessel bottlenecks, turbine supply delays, and soaring interest rates that struck fixed-bid auction power contracts lacking inflation indexation. The inability to pass through cost increases resulted in over DKK 40B in cumulative impairments and project cancellations (notably Ocean Wind 1 in the US), forcing dividend suspensions and asset disposals. Reported multi-cycle ROCE collapsed to -14.2% in 2023 and only recovered to 4.5%-5.4% in 2024-2025, completely failing the 12% ROIC and pricing power >= inflation hurdles.
column20: Fails Gate 3 (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Offshore wind pioneer exposed to catastrophic project delivery risks. Fixed-price power purchase and auction contracts demonstrated zero pricing power when turbine, vessel, and capital costs spiked, resulting in DKK 26.8B+ in write-downs in 2023, US project abandonments, and dividend cancellation. Multi-cycle ROCE (-14% in 2023, ~5% in 2024-2025) fails the 12% threshold.
column21: In FY2023, Ørsted posted an impairment charge of DKK 26.8B primarily from stopping development on US Ocean Wind 1, driving reported ROCE to -14.2%. Even adjusted ROCE fell from 12.9% in 2023 to 10.1% in 2024 and 8.4% in 2025, while reported ROCE was 4.5% (2024) and 5.4% (2025). Net interest-bearing debt expanded to DKK 58B in 2024 before asset sales and rights issue restructuring reduced it in 2025. The core business lacks pricing power against construction and financing inflation.

column14: Statutory regional water and sewerage monopoly licences for South West Water, Bristol Water, and SES Water covering southwest and southern England. Tariffs and revenue allowances are set by Ofwat under five-year regulatory determinations (PR19, PR24) with explicit CPIH inflation indexation applied to the Regulated Capital Value (RCV), ensuring theoretical tariff pricing power indexed to inflation.
column20: Fails Gate 4 (Competitive Advantage Period CAP = 10, REJECT). Regulated regional water monopoly. While statutory licences possess CPIH inflation indexation, traditional regulated utilities have a low industry persistence anchor (Tier 4, baseline 5-10Y). South West Water faces terminal regulatory and environmental headwinds following chronic sewage discharges, the Brixham cryptosporidium parasite contamination of drinking water, £24M+ in Ofwat redress enforcement, and criminal court fines. Intense societal and political pressure threatens severe regulatory ring-fencing, capping predictable runway to 10 years.
column21: Pennon's median GAAP ROIC is 3.87% across FY2022-2025 (FY22: 3.59%, FY23: 4.15%, FY24: 2.26%, FY25: 5.73%), reflecting Ofwat's allowed real CPIH WACC of ~4.0%. Net debt rose past £3.6B against £91.5M FY25 net income (and net losses in FY23-FY24). Under Ofwat PR24 determinations, Pennon accepted an ambitious £3.2B capex program for AMP8 requiring a £490M rights issue in early 2025 to repair leverage. Severe operational failures—including sewage spill sanctions and the 2024 Brixham boil-water parasite emergency—have permanently degraded political and regulatory tolerance, capping CAP at 10 years.

column14: Statutory regional water and wastewater monopoly licence in the English Midlands. Regulated capital value (RCV) formulaically indexed to CPIH inflation with zero customer churn. Primary erosion threats: regulatory price reviews (Ofwat PR24/AMP8), tightening environmental compliance standards, and political pressure over sewage overflows.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). While Severn Trent operates an essential regional water monopoly with best-in-class Ofwat operational delivery, the regulated utility business model caps ROIC at ~5-6% and requires perpetual heavy capital expenditure (£14.9B totex for AMP8) that far exceeds depreciation. Balance sheet carries £9.1B of debt (39x net income) with interest coverage of only 1.84x, requiring continuous debt market access and periodic equity dilution, failing Munger's peace-of-mind balance sheet standard.
column21: Regulated water and sewerage monopoly serving 4.8 million customers across the English Midlands. FY2024 revenue of £2,426.7M and operating profit of £702.5M. 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 5.8% (5.0%-6.3%), reflecting Ofwat allowed WACC. Net debt of £8,077.5M against TTM Net Income of £229.4M results in Net Debt / NI of ~35x, with LT Debt / NI of 39.5x. EBIT / Interest coverage of 1.84x (£702.5M / £382.4M) fails the >5.0x infrastructure threshold. Heavy capex burden (£1,592.8M vs £454.4M D&A) for AMP8 water quality and storm overflow remediation ensures persistent negative free cash flow after growth capex, violating Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency requirements.

column14: Statutory regional monopoly licence providing water and wastewater services across North West England. Formulaic RCV indexation to CPIH inflation provides inflation pass-through with captive regional customer base. Key risks include Ofwat regulatory tightening, environmental fines over storm overflows, and political scrutiny.
column20: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). United Utilities possesses an entrenched statutory water and wastewater monopoly in North West England with CPIH-linked revenue indexing. However, regulatory allowed ROIC is capped at ~5.5%, and the business faces perpetual capital dilution with AMP8 requiring ~£13B in totex. Balance sheet leverage is excessive with £11.2B in debt (19x net income) and interest coverage of 2.98x, failing the >5x infrastructure threshold and violating Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency requirements.
column21: Statutory water and wastewater provider serving 7.4 million people in North West England. FY2025 revenue of £2,616.3M and operating profit of £1,172.9M. 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 5.55% (4.04%-7.94%), anchored by Ofwat regulated cost of capital. Total long-term debt of £11,235.4M and net debt of £9,441.1M against TTM net income of £586.8M yields a Debt / Net Income ratio of 19.1x. EBIT / Interest coverage of 2.98x (£1,172.9M / £393.9M) falls well below the 5.0x minimum threshold for infrastructure assets. Capex of £1,535.0M exceeds D&A (£500.5M) by 3x, with ~£13B AMP8 commitments ensuring persistent negative post-capex free cash flow and perpetual reliance on debt capital markets.
